## How to use this file

**Owner:** read *NOW* and *OWNER QUEUE*. Everything you need to do is there, in order, with nothing
else mixed in.

**Agent:** read *NOW* and *AGENT QUEUE*. Run the top item. When finished, write a report into
*SESSION LOG* at the top, move the task into *DONE* with one line, and update *CURRENT STATE* with
measured figures. ⛔ Do not create a new session-report file — P5 established those fold in here.

**Assistant (chat):** read the newest *SESSION LOG* entry, update *CURRENT STATE*, move finished
items to *DONE*, add new work to the queues, and record confirmed decisions in *DECISIONS*.

**Row IDs (10-01):** owner rows are **O##**, agent rows **A##** — always with the letter. O34–O40 and
A34–A40 were different tasks and were confused for a whole session. In SESSION LOG and DONE, the older
wording "queue N" means **AN** and "OWNER N" means **ON**; those entries are history and are not rewritten.

⛔ **NUMBERING (10-02, owner): the A## sequence belongs to the owner and the chat assistant.** An agent may mark an A row done, correct its facts or flag it wrong — it may NOT add A rows. ⭐ **Findings an agent raises are F##**, numbered independently (F1, F2, …). A51/A52 and A66–A70 both collided because agents extended the A sequence; F1 and F2 were first numbered A66 and A67.

⛔ **CURRENT STATE is re-derived, never carried forward** — and the rules in `CLAUDE.md` § "What may go in
this repository" apply to every line written here.

**At handover:** delete *AGENT QUEUE*, *OWNER QUEUE* and *SESSION LOG*. What remains — current
state, decisions, done, and the doc directory — is the handover document.

**⚠ BUG — BOILERPLATE COUNTS AS SKILLS** (owner 10-31: *"yes to the boilerplate"*). "CDN" ≈ 564 postings, "Interpretability" a senior riser, "Attention" linked inside "Attention to detail": company text repeated in every posting (about us, benefits, EEO, legal) is matched as if it were the job's requirements. **Fix, in the ONE `postingMatcher` (so board stats, Your map, role / family maps and D114 spans all clean together, and D118's live counts inherit it):** (1) **strip repeated text before matching** — split a description into sentences; a sentence (normalised) that appears in ≥ 30 % of a company's active postings (and ≥ 3 postings) is that company's boilerplate and is not matched; kept per company, refreshed with the crawl; (2) **weight the requirements** — when the description has a requirements / qualifications / "what you'll bring" / "you have" section, skills are counted from it (and the responsibilities section); text before the first such heading, and benefits / EEO / "about us" sections, are not counted; no headings → step (1) only; (3) **concept nodes** (D115's 373) are matched only as whole terms with their exact casing when shorter than 5 characters, and never inside a longer common phrase listed in one file ("attention to detail", "data-driven", "fast-paced" …). **Measure and report before / after in NOW:** CDN, Interpretability, Attention, and the top 20 nodes by count. **TESTS:** `boilerplateStrippedPerCompany` · `requirementsSectionCounted` · `benefitsAndEeoNotCounted` · `shortConceptExactCase` · `commonPhraseNotLinked` · `matcherOneCopy`.

### ▶▶▶▶ OWNER REQUEST 10-19 — A MINIMAL EXTENSION, AND THE BOARD CARD'S BUTTON BOX. The top item when the owner says *"pick up the worklog"* (the earlier field-report block stays; this changes the extension's SURFACE, not its logic).

**The owner's words, from two screenshots.** **(1) The board:** *"look at the shade of the box holding the buttons on the job posting — the three buttons (ATS, star, Draft) have a shade that looks like a choppy box holding all three. We have to fix this."* **(2) The extension dock:** *"all the permissions, all the stuff that leads up to the reading of the page, the filling, everything else — they need to be POP-UPS and that's it. As little text on the widget as possible: too much text, too many lines, too many colours, and it looks choppy. As minimal as possible, only the necessary stuff, in minimal ICONS, not text. The floating panel that opens and closes should be a SQUARE BOX WITH THE DRAFT LOGO and that's it — just like the /d button on the job posting; click it to open and close. Any permission-related stuff and anything else moves to the extension's SETTINGS PAGE, which opens when we have to change a setting."* **What the screenshot of the dock shows (to remove or move):** a green toast-in-the-body *"Filled — review and submit"* with a ×; a standing sentence *"Filling by hand — a résumé on cue"* with a *Draft it instead* button; four text tabs *Fill · ATS · Résumé · Copy sheet*; a heading *"Review before you submit"*, a count sentence *"6 of 28 filled · 22 need you · 0 to check"* and *"Draft never submits for you."*; rows with a paragraph each (*"A cover letter — draft holds none for this job; attach one on the page, or skip it"*; *"None of the page's choices is close — pick it yourself"*); *"Remember for next time"*, *copy*, *use it*, *Skip* as text buttons; a footer *"Not ready — 22 need you. Submit the form yourself when you are happy with it."* and a text *I submitted it*. **Five header icons, three colours of banner, six dividers.**

**THE DESIGN RULES (T26) — every one is a test.** **TEXT BUDGET:** the dock body carries **only field labels and values** — **no sentences.** Every explanation, instruction and message is a **tooltip** or a **popup** (T27). **COLOUR BUDGET:** one neutral surface + **ONE accent (the brand orange)** + at most **one small status mark per row**; **no tinted banners, no coloured boxes for messages.** **LINE BUDGET:** **one** divider (under the header); groups are separated by **spacing**, not borders; **no row borders.** **ICONS, NOT WORDS:** header → *move, dock side, pop out, minimise, settings (gear), close* (no text); **tabs → four icons** (*Fill, ATS, Résumé, Copy sheet*) with tooltips and `aria-label`s; row actions → **icon buttons** (*use it* = ✓, *copy* = ⧉, *skip* = ⤖, *remember* = a small pin toggle); the footer → **one icon button** (*I submitted it*) and a **count badge** (a number, not a sentence). **A status is a SHAPE and a colour, not a sentence:** ✓ filled · ! needs you · ↺ to check (shape cues work in every theme, D91). **D60 (no pills), D91 (all four themes), D92 (at most two surface levels, never clip a shadow).**

**T27 · POPUPS FOR EVERYTHING THAT LEADS UP.** **A single reusable POPUP component in the dock's module family (`extension/popup-layer.js`)** for: **first-run consent**, **every permission request** (*Allow draft on Greenhouse / this site*), **"Read this page?"**, **ask-once** (*"Draft this job and queue its résumé, or just fill this form yourself?"*), **the résumé choice** (attach tailored / my résumé / generate / skip), **errors** (*"Résumé generation is unavailable"*), **confirmations** (*"I submitted it?"*), and **success toasts** (*Filled — review and submit*). **Rules:** **ONE popup at a time, queued**; **≤ 1 line of text and ≤ 2 icon-or-short-word buttons**; **informational toasts AUTO-DISMISS (3–4 s) and never sit in the body**; **a question stays until answered**; Esc closes it; **focus moves into it and returns after**; **`permissions.request` stays inside the click** (T12/T13/J13); a **Settings** link on a popup deep-links to the relevant section of the settings page (T29). **The dock body contains NONE of these.** **Tests:** no popup text is ever in the dock body · two events at once = a queue, not a stack · a toast dismisses itself and a question does not · a permission prompt is requested from its button's click · keyboard-operable · four themes.

**T28 · THE LAUNCHER — a square box with the draft mark, and nothing else.** **When the dock is closed it is a SQUARE BUTTON showing only the draft mark, the SAME shape, depth and orange as the board's /d button.** **Click: open; click again: close.** It **sits on a screen edge, drags along it, snaps back to it, and remembers its place per site.** **No text, no number** — at most a **small dot** when something needs the user. **The toolbar icon toggles the same dock** (the old slim bar is retired). **Mounts in the TOP frame only (T17)**; never covers a form field (it moves away from the field in focus); keyboard-reachable with a visible focus ring and an accessible name. **Tests:** closed = one square button, no text · click toggles · position remembered per site · never in a child frame · the toolbar icon toggles it · four themes.

**T29 · THE SETTINGS PAGE TAKES EVERYTHING ELSE.** **The extension's Options page becomes the ONE home for:** the **permission and consent** state (the per-site list; the preset hosts; *Always read here* sites; Greenhouse / Workday / Lever / Ashby / Workable / SmartRecruiters; revoke), **the four auto switches** (Read · Prepare · Capture to my account · Fill), **the disclosure text**, **"When I press Draft: queue the résumé automatically / ask me"**, **"In a manual fill: offer a résumé on cue / never"**, **saved answers** (a link to the web app's list), **the 90-day review reminder**, **developer details (T6)**, **Unlink / disconnect**, **shortcuts**. **The dock reaches it through the gear icon, and every popup's Settings link deep-links to its section (`options.html#permissions`, `#auto`, `#answers`)** — *"it opens when we have to change a setting."* **The page follows the same minimal rules** (plain section headings, one switch per setting, a one-line description under each). **Tests:** every setting that used to sit in the dock is reachable here · each deep link opens its section · the dock has no setting left in it · revoking a permission here removes it · four themes.

**T25 · THE BOARD CARD'S BUTTON BOX (the choppy shade).** **Symptom (Full House, every card):** a **darker rectangle behind the ATS, star and Draft buttons** — a box holding all three, a different shade from the card. **It is the D92 defect again: the cluster's wrapper paints its own fill, or clips the buttons' shadows and the orange glow at its own edge (an `overflow`), so the cut-off glow reads as a box.** **P0:** inspect the wrapper (`elementsFromPoint` on and around the cluster; computed `background`, `box-shadow`, `overflow`). **Fix:** the wrapper has **no fill, no border, no shadow, and clips nothing** (padding, or `clip-path: inset(-Npx)`), the three buttons sit **directly on the card**, **at most two surface levels** (D92 rule 1). **Tests:** the D92 **seam test** gains the cluster — background luminance just outside each button's edge equals the card's, in **all four themes and both card sizes** · no element around the cluster has `overflow` ≠ visible with a shadow larger than its padding · the orange glow is not clipped. **Also sweep every other group of buttons on a card or a row** (the deck, Draft House, The Table) for the same wrapper.

**✅ T25 DONE 10-22 (43n) — `1e84d1e`, local `main`, NOT pushed.** ⚠ The label collides with 43k's T25 (near-match saved answers, `t25NearMatchSavedAnswers`); this one is written **T25 (10-19)**. **P0 measured** in headless Chrome on the real `JobBubble.css`: the wrapper paints nothing — the box was **`.jb__rail { overflow: hidden }`** (the 0 → 196px reveal's clip) with **2px of room at the sides, 8px below**, against shadows reaching 8px (rest), 24px down (hover) and 9px of orange (Draft): luminance **243 243 → 247 in one pixel 8px under each square**, and **no shadow at all beside the last one**. **Fix:** `clip-path: inset(-10px -20px -28px -20px)` (the reveal still clips; every shadow and the focus ring have room) + `visibility` riding the reveal so the collapsed squares can't catch the pointer. **The sweep:** Draft House `.dh-rail` and The Table `.ah__rail` were the same rail with the same clip — same fix; `JobCard` (landing / database panel) is off the board, unchanged. **Tests +5** (`test/t25CardRailSeam.test.js`): the rule, the sweep, and **the seam test** — 4 themes × 3 / 2 per row / phone × card / ATS / Draft hovered, compared pixel for pixel with the card drawn with nothing clipping the rail: **old CSS fails 36 / 36, new passes 36 / 36.** Before / after screenshots were taken in the session (scratchpad, not committed). **Next: T26** (the dock surface), then T27 / T28 / T29, T30 last.

**OWNER DECISION 10-23 (later) — ONE LEVER, EVERY SITE.** *Owner: "all the reads automatic, a SINGLE lever instead of a lever for each website — there are hundreds of websites and a lever for each makes no sense; the user chooses once to accept automatic reading on any website, we seek his permission, and then it is fully automatic."* **This REPLACES the per-site model** of D97's preset list, T12's *Always read here* and T29's per-site list, **and it SIMPLIFIES T33: there is now ONE permission, requested once.** *(The 10-15 decision already added the OPTIONAL host pattern `https://*/*`; this asks for it whole, from one switch, instead of origin by origin.)*

**T35 · THE ONE LEVER.**
- **WHAT THE USER SEES.** Settings → Permissions: **ONE switch — *Read job pages automatically, on every website.*** **Off until the user turns it on.** Turning it on **IS the consent:** the plain disclosure (*what is read:* only pages that look like a job or an application — the job's title and company and the form's question labels; *never:* anything typed, any password or payment field; *what is sent:* the labels, to match the user's answers; *kept:* 30 days, on the computer) **and ONE Chrome permission prompt for all https sites** (`permissions.request({ origins: ['https://*/*'] })`, from the click on the settings page — the owner's 10-23 decision (a)). **The first-use popup (T27) asks in one line — *Allow* (opens the settings page at `#permissions`, where the one click requests it) / *Not now*.**
- **WHAT IT TURNS ON:** **Read and Prepare, automatically, on every site.** **Capture-to-my-account and Fill stay their own switches under it, default OFF** (D97's switches 3 and 4 — the owner may ask to turn either on).
- **THE DETECTOR — the heart of the guardrails.** **A tiny content script registered for `https://*/*`** decides **LOCALLY** whether a page looks like a job posting or an application — a JSON-LD `JobPosting`, a known ATS host or ATS frame, a URL pattern (`/careers`, `/jobs`, `/apply`), form heuristics (a résumé upload; name + email + phone) — **and on EVERY OTHER PAGE it does NOTHING: it reads no content beyond its own checks, makes no request, writes no storage, and does not keep the address — *"a page that is not a posting sends nothing, not its address, not a hash"* (the Web Store listing's promise) STILL HOLDS.** **Only when the detector says yes does the full read, prepare and (if switched on) capture run, and the launcher square (T28) appears ONLY on those pages — never an orange square on every website.**
- **GUARDRAILS.** A **built-in sensitive denylist** — banking and finance, health, email, government, social networks, password managers, and **LinkedIn / Indeed / Glassdoor** — where **nothing runs** · **`https` only**; nothing on `chrome://`, extension or `file:` pages · **skips every password and payment field and never reads a typed value** · **not in incognito** unless the user allows it in Chrome · **a *Never on this site* exception list** (per-site OFF, in Settings and one icon in the dock — *per-site is now the exception, not the rule*) · **Pause (1 hour / today)** and a **kill switch** · **revoking** the permission (in Settings or in Chrome's site access) drops reading back to click-to-read.
- **PERFORMANCE BUDGET (a test).** The detector costs **≤ 5 ms** on a non-job page: **no MutationObserver and no timer on a non-job page beyond ONE idle check and a throttled history listener**; frames are entered only for **known ATS hosts or frames that contain a form** (T11). **Measured on 20 popular sites.**
- **SECURITY.** The script exposes **no message handler to the page's own scripts**; the only page bridge stays the one on `jobsviadraft.com` (D99). It runs in the isolated world; it injects nothing into a non-job page.
- **IF THE USER REFUSES THE BROAD PERMISSION:** **click-to-read** (the toolbar icon, the shortcut, the context menu) still works everywhere; **T12's per-site *Always read here* remains only as an ADVANCED option for a user who refuses the broad grant** (the owner may delete it).
- **LISTING AND PRIVACY — recorded for the upload (nothing is uploaded):** the optional host list now carries the broad pattern; **`MANIFEST_RATIONALE.md` justifies it as the single OPTIONAL permission behind ONE user-visible lever, with the detector's local-only behaviour**; `STORE_LISTING.md`'s single purpose and disclosure, and `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION.md`, are updated; **`docs/AUTO_READ_RISK_ANALYSIS.md` §4 is AMENDED — "opt-in per site" becomes "one lever, local detection, a denylist"; R3 (capture) and R4 (fill) keep their own switches.** **⚠ The Web Store gives a broad host permission an in-depth review (even optional) — accepted by the owner's decision; counsel's view requested.**
- **TESTS (each mutation-checked):** lever off → nothing runs anywhere · lever on → a careers site on no list is read **with no prompt** · **a non-job page: no read, no request, no storage write, no launcher** · a denylist page: nothing · a page with a password field: skipped · incognito: nothing · a *Never on this site* site: nothing · Pause stops it all · the permission refused → click-to-read still works · the detector's time budget holds · page scripts cannot reach the content script · Capture and Fill stay off until switched on · the manifest's only broad pattern is the optional one (pinned).

**T15 · ONE TRUTH FOR "PREPARED".** The popup must show the **server packet's real state** (its id, when it was made, when it expires) — never a local count standing in for it. **An expired or absent packet is shown as *"Prepared 6h ago — expired"* — or, better, is RE-PREPARED SILENTLY the moment it is needed.** **Fill on a bound job NEVER fails with "Nothing is prepared"**: it re-prepares from `TabState` (T13), then fills. **Test:** a packet 6 h old → Fill re-prepares and fills in one press; a bound tab with no packet → the same; the popup's count equals the packet's.

**T24 · THE INTENT MODEL — how the extension knows which path the user is on (owner: *"what other tells do we have to do this accurately?"*).** `TabState` gains **`mode: 'drafted' | 'manual' | 'view'`** and **`intent`**, set by the strongest tell present, **in this order of authority:** **(1) the CONTROL pressed** — Draft vs Fill vs the résumé row — explicit, always wins · **(2) the BOARD'S INTENT** — `openPosting(job, intent)` carries **`apply`** (from the board's Draft / Apply) or **`view`** (Open posting) through the bridge into `TabState` · **(3) SEQUENCE on this tab** — Draft before any fill → `drafted`; a fill started or `filled > 0` → `manual` (Draft pressed AFTER that *tracks* the application, it does not regenerate a résumé that is already attached) · **(4) PAGE TYPE** — a posting page with no form allows only Draft; an application form allows both · **(5) the JOB'S SERVER STATE** — already drafted or queued in Draft House (never queue twice; show its state), the account's apply mode and its holds (a portal with a sign-in wall is **semi only**, the gated hand-off of D36) · **(6) a RÉSUMÉ already known** — one exists for (job, base-résumé hash) → attach, never regenerate; a generation in flight → show its progress and attach when ready, never start a second · **(7) the RÉSUMÉ FIELD** — present or absent, required or optional, already holding a file (the page shows a name) → skip · **(8) the ALLOWANCE** — *0 of 10* Draft slots → say so BEFORE queuing · **(9) the USER'S SETTINGS** — *When I press Draft: queue the résumé automatically (default) / ask me* and *In a manual fill: offer a résumé on cue (default) / never*. **When the tells disagree or are absent: ASK ONCE — *"Draft this job and queue its résumé, or just fill this form yourself?"* — with *Remember my choice*.** ⛔ **No adaptive guessing from past behaviour: the model is deterministic, so the same tells always give the same path.** **The dock states the path in words — *"Drafted — résumé queued, ready in about 40 s"* / *"Filling by hand — a résumé on cue"* — with a one-press switch.** **Tests (each mutation-checked):** Draft before any fill queues exactly ONE drafted application and ONE generation · a second Draft press queues nothing more · Fill with no Draft never generates until the user presses at the résumé row · Draft AFTER a fill with a résumé attached does not regenerate · the board's `apply` vs `view` intent sets `mode` through the bridge · a generation in flight is joined, not duplicated · *0 of 10* slots is said before queuing · full auto is still refused · a portal sign-in wall gives the semi path · the two settings change the behaviour · conflicting tells ask once and remember · the dock names the path.

| A32 | ⛔ **Legal: terms, disclaimer, liability waiver** | **The candidate is responsible for what their résumé claims.** Users can overstate; models can hallucinate; neither should land on us. Needs Terms of Service · acceptable use · limitation of liability and indemnity · an explicit AI-output disclaimer · and the privacy policy aligned with all of it. ⚠ **Neither I nor the agent is a lawyer** — draft the structure and plain-language clauses, then have it reviewed before it goes live.<br><br>✅ **DONE 10-01 (audit item 7): removed from the landing page, login and footer; kept only as an operational notice inside the auto-apply flow and the deck's Draft toast.** ✅ **O10-01: the marketing lines are DITCHED** — *"nothing is submitted until you approve it"* and *"it will not claim anything you did not"* are not a selling point worth holding. They currently ship in display type on the landing page (A31) and must come out. That also **removes the terms-vs-marketing contradiction**, so the waiver can be written plainly.<br><br>⛔ **WHAT ACTUALLY APPLIES, and two of three are live TODAY:**<br>• **Trader status governs CONSUMER CONTRACT LAW** — mandatory contact disclosure, withdrawal rights on paid digital services, and unfair-terms rules. Under the EU Unfair Contract Terms Directive a blanket "not liable for anything" clause against a consumer is **likely unenforceable however it is worded**. ⚠ Almost none of this bites yet: no entity, no payments, free, non-trader declared. **It arrives the moment money moves** — so the declaration changes in the same pass as `monetisationEnabled`, and the waiver should be drafted for the trader case rather than rewritten later.<br>• ⛔ **GDPR APPLIES REGARDLESS of trader status** — free or paid, entity or individual, to anyone processing EEA residents' personal data. There is no geographic gate on signup.<br>• ⛔⭐ **WE STORE SPECIAL CATEGORY DATA.** The tokenization exclusion list names `gender`, `ethnicity`, **`veteran_status`**, **`disability_status`**, plus `work_auth` and `visa_type`. Under **GDPR Article 9**, ethnic origin and health data are special categories requiring **explicit consent** on top of a normal lawful basis, with heightened retention, purpose-limitation and onward-transfer obligations. They exist because US employers ask EEO questions and the resolver needs answers — a legitimate reason that does not remove the obligation. **This is the most concrete current exposure and should be reviewed BEFORE the terms page.**<br><br>⚠ **AND THE PART NO DOCUMENT FIXES: there is no LLC, so there is no corporate veil.** A claim over a fabricated résumé claim, or a breach of those columns, reaches the owner **personally**. A disclaimer lowers the chance a claim succeeds; an entity limits what a successful one can reach. The owner's stated bar is ~1000 applications before incorporating — ⛔ **the exposure started when the first real résumé with a disability field was stored**, not at a volume number |

⛔ **Owner-only business, legal and financial material is kept out of the repo entirely** (`CLAUDE.md` §
"What may go in this repository"). Do not restate it here and do not put product tasks there.

**The three that touch engineering, and only these:**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **GDPR / Article 9** | `gender`, `ethnicity`, `veteran_status`, `disability_status` are stored. **Applies today** — no entity, payment or trader threshold. Affects consent UI, retention and the cross-service flow to Resume Master |
| **Monetisation gates** | The flag stays off until the entity, terms, privacy, processor and the trader declaration are all in place. Flipping it is not a code decision alone |
| **A42** | Recruiter domain gating is a product task, but what it *proves* is a legal question — see `LEGAL_AND_COMPLIANCE.md` |

⚠ **Where funding is concerned, the honest position: one real application sent, zero users,
`job_applications` empty.** That is pre-seed by any measure. ⭐ **The cheapest thing that changes it
is not more product — it is AF5 plus real users.** Investors fund evidence of demand, and there is
none yet because nobody has used it.

#### A57 · Resume Master's storage and backup (owner's note, 10-02 — moved here from inside the A57 row, words unchanged)

⛔⭐ **STORAGE AND BACKUP — do not treat the volume as a checkbox.** Resume Master has **no volume
today** (it was designed stateless). Railway allows **one volume per service**, so it needs its own,
mounted at **`/app/data`** to match draft's convention, with the code reading
**`RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH`** rather than a hardcoded path. ⚠ Adding it restarts the service.

⛔ **IT STARTS WITH NO BACKUP POLICY, AND IT WILL HOLD USER DATA.** draft's backup machinery was
hard-won: the budget is computed **from the volume**, it **refuses before the copy** rather than
filling the disk, and the retention bug that left a **12-day hole (09-17..09-29)** is fixed in
`b628ee6`. Resume Master would have none of that while holding **accounts, a credit ledger, and
résumés and PDFs the user explicitly asked to keep.** ⭐ **Those are not crawled rows — they are the
thing the user trusted us with, and they are unrecoverable.** Port draft's policy; do not write a
second one.

⚠ **SIZE IT FOR PDFs, NOT ROWS.** draft's volume sits at **481 / 1,000 MB** holding a job board, and
it already failed once with **ENOSPC at 481/500**. A few hundred stored résumés and generated PDFs
move faster than that. ⛔ **Decide the retention rule NOW, in this row:** stored artifacts expire
unless the user pins them — rather than discovering it at ENOSPC a second time.

⚠ **NAMING, and it is a live hazard:** draft's volume is called **`resume-master-volume`** — a
leftover from before the rename. ⛔ **Rename it BEFORE adding Resume Master's**, or the project will
hold two volumes where the one named after Resume Master belongs to draft. That is a 2am mistake
waiting to happen. Suggested: `draft-data` and `resume-master-data`.

## ⛔ OBSERVED IN PRODUCTION — 2026-09-29, first real generations

The first time anyone read real output end to end. **Seven findings, none blocking the domain move,
several blocking AF5.** Recorded so they are not lost in the split's momentum.

### ⛔ G1 · Generation invents content — AF5 unblocked by the owner 09-30 (supervised)

Agent-found. Two real documents said things the candidate never did: **Kafka, lifted from the job
ad**, and two unsourced responsibility bullets ("Collaborated with risk and infrastructure
teams…", "Instrumented service-level metrics…") plus an unsourced skill.

⛔ **The prompt forbids this. The claim guard only checks YEARS and SENIORITY, so both passed.**
Not new with the split — the same prompt draft always used. An unsupported-content check is queued.

⚠ Two samples on a deliberately thin test résumé show the problem exists; they do not give a rate.

✅ **Which prompt — answered 09-30, from the 09-28 run's own scripts** (`draft-e2e.mjs` and
`draft-e2e-save.mjs`, kept in that session's scratchpad): **both documents are `mode: "GENERATE"`** —
the standard Generate prompt, module `engineering`, the SAME request sent twice through draft's own
client, against a JD whose stack was "Go, Kafka". The first run listed **Kafka**; the second (the one
saved) invented the two responsibility bullets. ⛔ **Neither was A+.** The live verifier's generate
scenario ("Build services in Go.") mentions no Kafka and is not the source. So "A+ is deliberately
generative" is true and does not cover this: the prompt that fabricated is the one that says
"Generate bullets ONLY from the candidate's real experience". The owner's unblock of AF5 stands on
supervision — every document read before it is sent — not on the fabrication being A+'s.


### G2 · The generated résumé looks barely changed — owner-observed

Against the owner's real (thick) résumé, output reads close to the input. ⚠ **In tension with G1**,
which was measured on a thin one — a thin résumé may invite padding while a thick one gets almost
nothing. **Neither the change rate nor the invention rate is measured.** Both need a real sample,
not two anecdotes.

⛔ Open and unverified: **is generation even being triggered on the web route?** The usage record
from the owner's run is the check, and the agent is waiting to read it.

✅ **Answered, agent-measured 09-28 from both services' logs: YES.** The owner's run went
`/api/generate` → the tools service in 28.6 s, module `engineering`; the claim guard inspected 5,678
chars; `usage_events` got a `resume_generate` row (user 3, Sonnet 5, 3,979 in / 3,798 out,
**$0.0635**, a cold 7,009-token cache write); and the lift was recorded **42 → 58 (+16)**. Resume
Master's metering line matches to the token. So the model ran and the scorer saw a 16-point change —
"barely changed" is then a question about WHAT changed, which still needs the real sample above.

### ⛔ G3 · AG4's duplication defect is LIVE AGAIN

The generated résumé shows a role stated three times:

```
Stripe | Software Development Engineer, Payments Infrastructure Bangalore
Software Development Engineer, Payments Infrastructure        ← italic restatement
Bangalore
```

⛔ This is **exactly** AG4's shape, and AG4's tests pass: *"a model's plain-text restatement of the
header and bullets is read, not reprinted"* · *"a nested entry-header does not leak its date into
the body"*. **Green tests, live defect** — the eighth instance of that pattern. The tests assert
something narrower than the behaviour, or the path has changed under them.

Corroborated independently, agent 09-28: the agent's own second real generation (synthetic résumé,
Stripe role) extracted as `Stripe | Software Engineer 2021 - 2025 Software Engineer 2021 - 2025` and
`B.S. Computer Science 2021 B.S. Computer Science 2021` — the same role-restatement shape, on a
different résumé. Two independent documents, so it is not a one-off input.

### G4 · Formatting need not be a model call at all — and mostly already is not

⭐ **The owner is right, and it is closer to true than it looks.** Formatting is deterministic
(`resumeFormatter.js`). The LLM formatting pass is behind `RESUME_MASTER_LLM_FORMAT=1` and A2 found
**zero `resume_format` events ever** — it has never run.

⛔ But the stale artifact remains: `FORMATTING_SYSTEM` still carries **35 of the renderer's 43 CSS
lines describing a design the renderer ABANDONED**. So the prompt spends tokens on, and could
instruct a model toward, a layout that no longer exists.

⚠ **Correction, agent 09-28: that artifact is already gone.** A2 rebuilt `FORMATTING_SYSTEM` in Resume
Master FROM `RESUME_STYLE_BLOCK` (a test fails if its source restates any CSS), and A4 deleted
draft's copy along with the unused `server.js` stylesheet. What is left is only the decision below —
and it is now a decision about Resume Master's code, off by default and never run.

**Decide:** delete the LLM format path outright, or rebuild its prompt from the renderer's CSS.
Deleting is cheaper and nothing uses it.

### ⛔ G5 · The ATS panel shows a NUMBER and a BAND, and they read as contradictory

The panel shows **"ATS Score 58"** beside **"Strong match"**.

⛔ **The band is CORRECT** — the Strong cutpoint is 44 at 100% precision, and v4's median is 28, so
58 is comfortably Strong. **The defect is showing the number at all.** 58/100 reads as a failing
grade to a human; ρ = 0.746 supports coarse ordering and not a displayed figure; and the mobile
contract already marks `matchScore` **INTERNAL — DO NOT DISPLAY**. The desktop panel never got the
same treatment.

**Fix: show the band, drop the number.** `UI_REDESIGN.md` already says this; it is live today and
does not need to wait for the redesign.

### G6 · The generic-language classifier has gaps

A "Generic language" section exists and correctly holds *Managed, Partnered, Coordinated, Grew* —
but **"Defined" and "Created" are listed as MISSING VERBS**, and **"collaboration" as a MISSING
COMPETENCY**.

All three are things almost any candidate could claim, so surfacing them as gaps implies a
deficiency that is not real. ⛔ AH3 built exactly this suppression and set a specificity threshold;
these three sit the wrong side of it. Note the corpus head is **soft skills, not technologies** —
*collaboration* appears 199 times — so the threshold is under-tuned rather than absent.

### G7 · Resume Master's Railway URL errors in a browser — ⚠ CHECK BEFORE THE DOMAIN MOVE

`resume-master-production-d960.up.railway.app` returns an error when opened directly, while the
agent's live verifier passes **24 of 24 scenarios** against it.

⚠ **Most likely benign** — an API-only service has no route at `/`, so a bare visit 404s. But
⛔ **confirm what the root returns and that it is intentional BEFORE moving `resumemaster.one` onto
it.** A domain move onto a service that genuinely errors makes the failure public, and this project
has five precedents of a status code being read as evidence in the wrong direction.

✅ **Confirmed before the move, agent 09-28, with a browser's own request** (Chrome user-agent,
`Accept: text/html…`): `/` → **404 `application/json` `{"error":"not_found"}`**, and `/favicon.ico` and
`/robots.txt` the same. INTENTIONAL: the service has no root route, its catch-all answers every
unknown path with a JSON 404 by design (the opposite of draft's SPA catch-all), and that is declared
in the contract (`x-not-found`) and pinned by two envelope-harness scenarios. A browser renders it as
raw JSON on a 404 — which reads as an error, and is not one. ⚠ Consequence accepted: since step 4,
anyone opening `resumemaster.one` sees that JSON. A human-facing root is a contract change (a route,
so a version bump) if ever wanted.

✅ **Re-confirmed 09-29 by SCREENSHOT in real Chrome** (headless, driven by puppeteer): both
`https://resumemaster.one/` and the Railway URL render Chrome's JSON viewer showing
`{"error":"not_found"}`, HTTP 404, no page title, no failed sub-requests; `/v1/version` on the same
domain renders 200 with `service: "resume-master"`. **Owner decision: keep the JSON 404.** Closed.

## STANDING RULES

Prepend to every agent task.

```
Session-aware: read by SYMBOL, not line number. Regression-proof: dependents and children in the
SAME pass with verdicts. Migrations additive + dual-path, byte-identical in BOTH runners, and
transactional. Re-derive the test baseline first; introduced failures must be 0.

⛔ A 200 IS NOT EVIDENCE. The SPA catch-all answers 200 with index.html for any unknown path and has
produced a false finding FIVE times. Assert a specific JSON key.

⛔ A GUARD NEVER SEEN TO FAIL IS NOT EVIDENCE. Seven have shipped inert. Verify by INJECTING a
violation.

⛔ SCREENSHOT ANYTHING USER-VISIBLE. In one session four things were green and wrong: a policy a
single request falsifies, a harness scoring unweighted while labelling itself weighted, a guard
proving a sweep complete on the one component it could not see, and two tests REQUIRING the legacy
brand to stay.

⛔ NO sed -i, NO Python whole-file writes on server.js or scripts/migrations.js. The byte-identity
tests depend on line endings and the failure shows as CLEAN in git diff. Three incidents.

⛔ WHERE A PREMISE IS WRONG, SAY SO AND MEASURE. Three briefs in a row had their central premise
inverted by the first measurement, and each time that was the most valuable thing in the session.
```

### D42 · ⛔⛔ TAGGING MADE THE BOARD WORSE. Prove the tags before any UI leans on them.

✅ **BUILT 10-06 (32), `e57d930`, local.** Measured on the 10-06 local board (2,616 rows, the tagger in memory, read-only — production reads refused): **H1 IN** — `finance` was the job FUNCTION (18 rows: tax directors, controllers); the 189 fintech-sector engineers carry `engineering`. **Owner, in-session:** domain (the job's work) and sector (the employer's) are DIFFERENT tags — domain stays the sentence's word; **sector** (`shared/companySectors.js`, a closed company list, 35 companies) is a drawer filter. **H2 IN** — a chosen domain replaces the scope (D30); **owner: "all" = engineering + data** (`ROLE_SCOPE_EXTRA`; every other profile keeps its bucket). **H3 OUT** — Boston recall 5/5 on the raw strings; the one metro miss was "Seattle WA" with no comma (fixed; TAGGER_VERSION → 2). **H4 IN** — the location's "unknown" admitted NON-US rows (716 of 902 kept for Boston) — fixed. Kept rows labelled ("1 in Boston · 32 with no city on file, shown after"), a **strict toggle** (strict_tags) in the panels, **"+ add" moved into the panel** (owner). Acceptance as a test on real strings (+8). ⚠ Not re-run on production (O76b-3). ⚠ Level / workplace dials still carry their coverage note; employment stays dimmed (unchanged).

**The owner's level-1 test.** Every other filter removed. **Boston alone. Finance alone.** ⛔ The jobs
they could ALREADY SEE — finance-sector engineering jobs, jobs in Boston — **disappeared, and
irrelevant jobs appeared in their place.** *"Plain stupid. I don't know if the tagging even worked or
if it did a worse job."*

⛔ **THE INVARIANT, stated once so it can be tested:** **applying a filter must never remove a row that
carries the tag it asks for.** Every row visible with no filter whose tag is F is visible with F
applied, and **known matches rank before kept-unknowns.** The owner's observation violates both.

#### The four hypotheses — rule each IN or OUT with evidence, in order. ⛔ Do not skip to a fix.

**H1 · The "finance" tag may not mean what the owner means.** ✅ **Owner, 10-06: *finance*, *data* and the rest are SUB-DOMAINS OF ENGINEERING.** The board holds only engineering, so the domain dial's values are its verticals and **"all" means no domain filter.** Yet `O72(a)` says finance has only **8 postings** by role family. So **what is the `finance` value derived from — the role, or the company's sector?** A **fintech engineer** is *engineering* by role and *finance* by sector. ⭐ **If `finance` is derived from the role, the filter returns a handful of finance-role rows and drops every finance-sector engineer — exactly the jobs the owner saw vanish.** Report **the domain tag's value set, what each value is derived from, and its precision and recall.** If sector is not a tag at all, it is a **missing dimension** rather than a bad one — add it at the **COMPANY** level, deterministic first (the company KB, known lists), then **export → tag → import** for the rest (D17).

**H2 · The domain dial REPLACES the profile's role scope instead of narrowing it.** ✅ **Decided 10-06 — this answers `O60(a)`: an unset domain reads "all", not "engineering".** The board is engineering throughout, so **`all` lifts the profile's role scope** and *finance*, *data* etc. **narrow** it. ⛔ **Verify the built behaviour matches:** with no domain set, **no role scope is applied**; with *finance* set, what remains is a **subset** of what was visible — never a different set.

**H3 · The location tagger misses real Boston rows.** `O60(b)` measured *"in Boston"* = **1 known
match + 32 country-only/remote kept after it.** **One** Boston match on a board where the owner can
see several means metro **recall is bad** — *"Boston, Massachusetts"*, *"Greater Boston"*,
*"Cambridge, MA"*, *"Boston, MA (HQ)"*, *"Remote — Boston"*. ⚠ **Coverage is not accuracy**: D29
reported metro at 91.7%, and a tagger can fill a column 100% with wrong values.

**H4 · Soft-null keeps unknown rows, and they surface among or above the known matches.** *"Kept,
not hidden"* was right for **honesty** and wrong for **relevance**. ⛔ **Report the composition of the
32 kept rows** — country-only? remote? a **different known metro**? ⛔ **Unknown is not different:** a
row tagged *New York* must be **excluded** for Boston; only a row with **no city on file** may be
kept — and it ranks after, labelled.

#### ⛔ What to report BEFORE any fix

Per tag value (Boston, finance, and every other dial value): **PRECISION and RECALL from a
hand-checked sample** — 50 rows carrying the tag and 50 rows the raw string suggests should carry it.
**List the false negatives by pattern.** ⛔ **Coverage alone is not evidence** — it is how this shipped.

#### Rules that hold whatever the evidence says

- **Narrowing never replaces scope.** · **Known matches rank first.** · **Kept rows are labelled and
  ranked after.** · **Unknown ≠ different.**
- ⭐ **The sentence and dial say exactly what happened:** *"1 in Boston · 32 with no city on file,
  shown after."* A count that blends the two is the lie.
- ⭐ Offer a **strict toggle** — *"only jobs known to be in Boston."*
- ⚠ Dials that cannot carry a filter must not look like they can: level **65.2%**, workplace
  **47.5%**, employment **7.7%**.

#### ✅ Acceptance — the owner's own test, as a test

**Boston alone** returns a **superset** of the Boston rows visible unfiltered · **finance alone**
returns the finance-sector jobs the owner saw · **both** return their **intersection, ranked** · each
reproduced against a **fixture of the real location strings**. ⛔ "The tags have 91% coverage" is not
an answer to this row.

### D41 · ⛔ THE CAPTURED JOB: not findable, no salary, no logo

✅ **BUILT 10-06 (32), `8caefbb`, local.** ⚠ The owner's capture was NOT looked up by job_id (production reads refused — O76b-1); the mechanism was found in the code: a capture with no POSITIVE US evidence was inserted, **held** (is_active 0) and **auto-starred** → in ★, not ALL. **(a)** which query backs each chip: ALL and ★ = one statement (★ adds `uj.starred = 1`, relaxes is_active — the labelled exception); /d = a separate query that hard-joined the role bucket and title filter. Now ALL admits the user's own rows (starred · drafted · captured), /d drops its hard narrowing, and a capture no longer stars. ⚠ /d's list is still its own endpoint → **A91**. **(b)** salary was lost in three places (the extractor's `Salary:` line dropped; JSON-LD `baseSalary` ignored; Ashby's summary strings ignored) — read deterministically now (`salaryText.js`), with the failing formats as fixtures. **(c)** logo queued at capture time from the employer's own site; never an ATS host. **(d)** no US evidence → refused before any write, two messages, recorded as `refused_not_us`; the route's 422 `error` is what every extension build shows — no release needed. +10 tests.

The owner captured a job. It was **in ★ but not in ALL**, so search never found it; they reached it only through the `/extension` page. It also had **no salary** (the original did) and **no company logo.** ⛔ **D33's acceptance is not met until all of it is fixed.** Start from `job_captures` and the URL.

⭐ **Production evidence, 10-06 (O43, read in the container).** `scraped_jobs` holds **no rows with source `import`** — only greenhouse 1,142 · ashby 650 · lever 65 · workable 1 — and `job_captures` holds **one** capture from a company that is not on the list: **`ashby/hims-and-hers`** (the owner's). ⚠ **Do not read the missing `import` source as proof the row is absent:** a capture of a known-ATS URL is refetched and may be stored under source `ashby` with origin `import`. **Look the capture's `job_id` up directly** and report, in order:

1. does a `scraped_jobs` row exist for it, and is it `is_active = 1`?
2. ⛔ **was it one of the 59 rows the O41 retire pass deactivated on 10-06?** That pass retires rows with no *positive* US evidence, and a bare-*Remote* capture has none — so it would sit in ★ (labelled *outside the US*) and vanish from ALL, which is **exactly what the owner saw.** Check the retire log for that `job_id`.
3. is there a `user_jobs` row, and what does it carry?
4. does it have tags and an `enriched_at`?

⚠ **Three different mechanisms** — *never inserted* · *inserted, then retired* · *active but excluded by ALL's query* — give the **same symptom and opposite fixes.** The model in (a) is the requirement either way; this says which bug produced it.

⚠ **And `hims-and-hers` is not on `company_ats_list`, so nothing re-crawls it.** A captured job from an unconfigured company is **never refreshed and can age out** — see `O75(g)`.

**(a) ROOT CAUSE, FOUND BY THE OWNER: ★ AND ALL ARE TREATED AS SEPARATE TABLES.** The capture was written to **★ (`user_jobs`)** and **not to the ALL view** — so ALL, and therefore search, never saw it. ✅ **THE MODEL, decided 10-06: ALL is the whole set. ★ Saved, /d Drafted and + Imported are SUB-TABLES of it — filtered views of ALL, not separate stores.** Everything a user stars, drafts or imports **is a row in ALL**, and each chip is **ALL plus a membership predicate.**

⛔ **Verify and report:** which query backs each of the four chips today, and **where the model splits.** ⛔ **Fix it structurally — one query, one card list, one predicate per chip** — rather than patching the capture path to write to a second place.

⛔ **Invariants, each a test:** every job in ★, /d or + **also appears in ALL** · search and every filter find it **there** · the ★ / /d / + results are **exactly** ALL's results restricted by the predicate — so a filter that hides a row in ALL hides it in ★ too.

⚠ **One labelled exception:** a starred job since **retired** (aged out, or the older *"outside the US"* saves) stays in ★ marked *no longer listed* — it is no longer an active row of ALL, and the existing labels already say so. State it in the report; do not let it break the invariant silently.

⛔ **A capture no longer auto-stars.** The gateway stars every capture today so it can be found; the `+` membership replaces that (D40). ★ is for what the user chose to save.

✅ With **(d)** below a non-US posting can no longer be captured at all, so the old question — *does a capture bypass the US gate?* (`O67(e)`) — is **closed: it does not.**

**(b) SALARY.** Re-fetch the captured URL and compare the live posting with the stored row. **Say where
it was lost:** the client text never carried it · the extractor missed the format (JSON-LD
`baseSalary`, *"$150,000 – $180,000 USD"*, hourly, *"150K–180K"*) · the normaliser rejected it · the
gateway **attached the capture to an existing row and did not donate the salary** (the donation path
exists) · or it is stored and not shown. ⛔ Fix **at the cause**, and add the failing format as a
fixture. Deterministic only — D17.

**(c) LOGO.** A77 fetches logos in the background from the employer's homepage. A company the board has
never crawled is **never queued.** ⛔ **Derive the company's domain from the capture** and queue the
fetch **at capture time**; show the letter tile until it lands. ⛔⛔ **Never use the ATS host's
favicon as the company's logo** — a Greenhouse mark on every Greenhouse job is the Clearbit-fallback
failure again, with a different provider.

**(d) NO US EVIDENCE → NO CAPTURE.** ✅ Owner, 10-06: *"if it lacks US evidence it shouldn't be captured at all"*, and **the extension must tell the user, in a popup, that the job is not based in the US.**

- **The server decides, the extension shows.** `POST /api/import/job` runs the US test **before** anything is written. On failure it writes **no job row and no `user_jobs` row**, answers a **refusal with a plain message**, and records the **attempt** in `job_captures` (`action = 'refused_not_us'`) so the owner can see what was turned away.

Use all of it. A posting that says only *"Remote"* is no longer a dead end if the page says *"US-based"* or lists a USD range.

- ⛔ **Tests:** a non-US page → refused, **zero rows written** · a bare-*Remote* page with a USD range → accepted · a bare-*Remote* page with **no** evidence → refused with the *couldn't confirm* message · the refusal is recorded and visible.

✅ **Acceptance:** (1) capture ONE US posting that states a salary → it is **in ALL**, found by its title within seconds, with the salary, and with a logo or a letter tile plus a queued fetch · (2) capture ONE non-US posting → the popup says so and **nothing** is written.

## ⛔ D45–D48 · OWNER BATCH, 2026-10-07 — load lag, dead cards, the sentence's type, the posting panel header

⏸ Queued 2026-10-07 by the owner, from the live site. ⛔ **Suggested place in the queue:** D45 goes **right after D42 and D41** — a board that shows nothing for seconds on every panel makes every other fix look broken. D46 follows D40 (it touches the same `+` view). D47 and D48 are UI and go last.

### D45 · ⛔ EVERY PANEL SHOWS AN EMPTY BOARD FOR THE FIRST SECONDS — on every switch, not just the first load

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (34), `3b57b50`, local.** **Measured first** (throwaway local server, 2,616 rows, headless Chrome, state stamped in the page): (1) the empty state rendered **while loading** — `shouldShowEmptyState` never looked at a request in flight (cold load: blank → EMPTY ~475 ms → cards ~600 ms); (2) a switch showed the **previous view's cards** until the answer; (3) facets fired **first** and, being synchronous board queries, held the board's request behind it (`/api/jobs` at +860 ms); (4) a cold load asked for the same page **twice**. ⚠ Nothing scores on the request path; server time per request is tens of ms since `62a89a9`. **Fixed:** skeletons in the card's geometry until the current view answers (never the empty state, never another view's cards) · a per-view cache with stale-while-revalidate and an idle prefetch of the other three views · facets after the board · one request per view at a time. **After:** cold load blank → skeleton 198 ms → cards 333 ms; at +300 ms per request no empty frame; warm switches ALL p50 16 / p95 24 ms · ★ 7 / 33 · /d 8 / 16 · + 11 / 13. ⚠ Production p50/p95 not measured (O78e). +4 tests.

The owner: *"any panel I open takes a second before it loads and shows empty for the first few seconds"* — ALL, ★, /d and `+`, **every time**, not only when the site opens.

⛔ **Two defects, and they need separate fixes:**

**1 · An EMPTY STATE IS SHOWN WHILE LOADING.** ⛔ This is **"silence reported as success"** — the board says *nothing here* when it means *not here yet*. Whatever the speed, **loading and empty must be different states**, and the empty copy must never render until a response has actually arrived and been empty.

**2 · THE FETCH IS SLOW, OR IS REPEATED NEEDLESSLY.** The production board is **1,858 rows** — a table that size should answer in tens of milliseconds, so *seconds* means something is wrong, not that the data is big.

**MEASURE FIRST, per panel — report the numbers before changing anything:**
- time to first byte and time to first card for each of ALL / ★ / /d / `+`, on production data
- **server time per endpoint** (`/api/jobs`, `/api/jobs/facets`, the draft and import queries) — ⚠ which one is slow
- **is it a waterfall?** profile → facets → jobs fetched one after another, when they could run together
- **does a switch refetch from scratch?** (the panel unmounts and loses its data) · is the same request made twice?
- ⚠ **does the server score or rescore on the request path?** `A52`'s migration 118 made stored reports stale once, and a board pass that scores per request would be slow *every* time, not once
- ⚠ **D41(a) just made ★, /d and `+` views of ALL** — if each is now a separate heavy query over ALL, four panels pay the cost four times

**THE FIXES, in this order:**
1. ⛔ **Never show an empty state while loading.** Skeleton cards in the card's own geometry from the first frame.
2. ⭐ **Stale-while-revalidate:** keep the previous panel's data on screen, mounted, and refresh behind it. Switching ALL → ★ → ALL should be **instant** the second time.
3. **Do not unmount panels on a switch.** The state the user built (the sentence, the search, the scroll position) survives.
4. **Fire requests together, not in a chain.** **Prefetch** the other views on idle, or on hover of their control.
5. **Fix the slow query itself** once measured — an index, a join that should not be there, or work that belongs off the request path.

⛔ **Do not mask a slow server with a spinner.** If a query takes seconds, the fix is the query; the skeleton is for the honest tens of milliseconds.

✅ **Acceptance:** switching between the four panels shows **content or skeletons in the first frame**, **never an empty state**, and a warm switch is instant. Report p50 and p95 per panel on production data. ⛔ Tests: **the empty copy does not render while a request is in flight** · a second visit to a panel renders from cache before the network answers.

### D49 · THE `StickyBar` MODULE — one sticky-at-the-top section, reused

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (34), `b590a5b`, local.** ⚠ **Found: the Full House bar did NOT stick** (measured 202 → −698 px) — and could not, because sticky works only inside its parent and the bar's parent was the short header. **`StickyBar`** (sticky against the nearest scroll container; stuck state from an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel — no scroll listener; blur + hairline + depth only when stuck; `--z-sticky`; reduced motion). The board's bar and sort panel moved to the top of `<main>` inside it. **Measured:** not stuck at rest or after 60 px; holds at 74 px and stuck deep in the list; keeps the sentence's column; the sort panel opens beneath it. A first-mount race (a mid-layout callback reporting "stuck" at rest) found and fixed. The posting action bar is the second consumer — with D48. +2 tests.

✅ Owner 10-07: *"use the same code modularly … make it a modular section that can be reused and reuse it here."*

**Extract it from the board.** The Full House bar already sticks to the top as the page scrolls. Lift that behaviour into **one component (or hook + CSS) — `StickyBar`** — and make **both** consumers use it: **the board's bar** and **the posting panel's action bar** (D48). ⛔ Two implementations of one behaviour is how the mark, the cards and the buttons all drifted.

**The module owns:**
- `position: sticky; top: 0` against **the nearest scroll container** — the page for the board, the panel's own scroll area for the posting — chosen by the consumer, never a hard-coded `window`.
- a **stuck state** (`is-stuck`), found with an **IntersectionObserver on a 1px sentinel** placed just before the bar — **not scroll listeners** — that adds the hairline and the shadow only when it is actually stuck.
- a translucent surface with a blur, so content passes under it legibly; a **named z-index token** (`--z-sticky`, above content and below `--z-nav`) — no literals.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: no transition on the shadow.

⛔ **Tests:** both consumers import the same module · the stuck class appears after scrolling past the sentinel and **not before** · the bar stays inside its container (it does not escape the panel) · removing the module breaks both. ⚠ **Sticky fails silently under any `overflow: hidden` ancestor** — so the test must render it in the **real panel**, not an isolated div. The sketch's tab 2 runs the board's bar on the same module.

## ⛔ D51–D54 · THE DRAFT → APPLY → CLEAR LOOP — 2026-10-07

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (37), local — NOT pushed (O80a).** D51 `2912adf` · D52 `d5b8047` (premise refuted — see SESSION LOG) · D53 `31cdc10` (migration 130) · D54 `b5303a0`. ⛔ The "per-company cap" D51 and D54 cite does not exist (O80b).

### D51 · ⛔⛔ A DRAFTED JOB IS SEEN NOWHERE, AND ITS BUTTON IS JUST GREYED OUT

The owner drafted a job. It is *"added or seen nowhere"*, the **Draft button is greyed out**, and there is no sign of where it went.

⛔ **Two defects in one click:** (1) the job cannot be found afterwards; (2) **a disabled button is a dead end** — it says *no* without saying *why* or *where to go.* Same class as D33's *"silence reported as success."*

**PROBE — trace ONE click and report, in order:**
1. **What the Draft click writes** — which table, which state, which user — and whether the response says so.
2. **Why the button is disabled:** already drafted · the quota (*"a Draft or a new résumé uses one"*) · or a cap (per-run / per-day / per-company). ⚠ Those mean three different things and need three different sentences.
3. **Does each place that should show it actually read it?** The **/d chip** (D41(a): ALL restricted to drafted) · **Draft House → Queued** · **The Table → In play** (D15). ⛔ D41(a) says /d is a sub-table of ALL — this may be **the same separate-store defect on the /d chip**, and D46(b) already found /d cards dead.
4. **Is the row hidden by scope** — the profile, the market gate, `is_active`?
5. **Did the quota decrement**, and does the UI say so?

**THE FIX, once measured:**
- ⛔ **A disabled Draft button never appears without a reason.** Its states: ✅ **APPROVED TREATMENT (owner, 10-07): the `/d` button INVERTED** — transparent fill, an accent border and glyph, a small ✓ at its corner — **not greyed out.** Clicking it opens the job's place in Draft House; a second action undoes it (→ D53) · *Out of drafts — resets in 3h* · *Per-company cap reached (3/3 at Scale AI)* · *Can't be drafted: <reason>.*
- ⛔ **One write, three readers** — /d, Queued and In play all read **the same row** (the D41(a) invariant), so a draft appears in all three at once.
- The card shows its new state **without a reload**; a refused draft says why and **writes nothing half-way.**

✅ **Acceptance:** draft one job → within a second it is in /d, Draft House → Queued and The Table → In play; the button reads *Drafted*; the quota shows one fewer; a reload keeps all of it. ⛔ **Tests:** each reader sees it · a refused draft shows its reason · the button is never disabled without one.

### D52 · ⭐ START THE QUEUE — nothing starts a drafted job today

Owner: *"I should be able to start the queued items for apply, where it starts generating résumés and tries to fill in the details as required — or at least have the data packet ready to be filled using the extension in semi."*

⛔ **Verify first:** a drafted job sits in Queued with **no control that starts it.** If a run can start only from somewhere else, say where.

**WHAT START DOES — per item, and as "Start queue" for all:**

```
QUEUED → PREPARING (résumé generated) → PREPARING (form found, fields resolved) →
   direct tier → FILLED, WAITING FOR YOUR APPROVAL      (semi: you approve each submit)
   gated tier  → PACKET READY — open the page, the extension fills it (⌃⇧Y), the review
                 overlay shows, YOU submit
   a step fails, or a question has no confident answer → STOPPED (D14), with the reason
```

- **Résumé generation is the one model call D17 allows.** ⚠ It uses the draft quota — **show the cost BEFORE starting:** *"Starting 5 uses 5 of your 10 résumés today."*
- Fields come from the **deterministic resolver.** ⛔ Eligibility fields are exact or flagged, **never guessed** (D36).
- **Start respects the caps and says so honestly:** *"4 of 7 will start now; Scale AI holds 2 (3/3 today); 1 waits for tomorrow's limit."*
- ⛔ **Unattended stays locked.** AUTO is **attended** — a human approves each submit — until D36 / O73 have both passed. The toggle may exist; it may not be flipped.
- ⛔ **The kill switch is checked per run before any model call**, and a **failed step leaves the item retryable** — a 429 or a timeout must not stamp it attempted.
- **Progress is visible per item** (the four dots, D14) — never a spinner with no state.
- ⚠ **A packet expires** (the extension's prepared packet lives ~10 minutes). One that lapses while the user is away must be **re-preparable with one click**, shown as *"ready — expires in 8 min / prepare again"* — never silently dead.

✅ **Acceptance:** queue three, press Start; each reaches *filled-awaiting-approval*, *packet ready* or *stopped-with-reason*, and **none stays "queued" without saying why.** Report the real result for **one job per tier.**

### D53 · ⭐ REVIEW AND CLEAR — with a 7-day recycle bin

Owner: items queued for review must be **reviewable and clearable**, and — ✅ **corrected 10-07: removal already works** (the owner can remove items when needed), so this row does not add it; it **makes it recoverable.** *"If I applied it would be moved to that section; if I didn't and am not anymore I should be able to clear them — a 7-day recycle bin if users want to go back."*

**THE RULE:**

```
APPLIED (you submitted)         → moves to The Table (D15). History. Not clearable here.
NOT APPLIED, no longer wanted   → CLEAR → recycle bin for 7 days → then purged
NOT APPLIED, still wanted       → stays in Queued / Stopped / Ready
```

- **Review.** Every *ready to review* item opens to its résumé and its prepared fields — **exceptions first** (D14) — with **Approve · Skip · Clear.**
- **Clear** — ✅ **removal already exists and works** (owner, 10-07). **Find it and build on it — do not add a second one.** What changes: it becomes **soft** (to the bin), it gains **multi-select** and *"clear everything older than 7 / 30 days"*, and ⛔ **it behaves the same in every non-terminal state** — report any state where it is missing or behaves differently. ⚠ **Today's removal is probably a HARD delete — verify.** If so, the bin means converting it, and **anything removed before the bin exists is gone**: say so plainly rather than implying it can be restored.
- **The recycle bin lives inside Draft House** — a *Cleared · 7 days* fold under Queued, **not a new nav item.** It shows the count, and per item *"purges in N days"*, **Restore** (back to its exact prior state, résumé intact) and **Delete now.**
- ⛔ **Clearing is a SOFT delete** (`cleared_at`, `purge_after`) — never a hard delete in the click path. It removes the **queue entry**, never the posting (D43: a posting a user has a relationship with is never hard-deleted).
- ⛔ **The purge needs a MECHANISM, not just a policy:** a **scheduled sweep**, plus a **read-time filter** so an expired item is invisible even if the sweep runs late. A57's lesson: a retention rule enforced only at read time is a policy with no mechanism. ⛔ **The sweep carries the brake the 1,288-row `cleanup_log` id 85 deletion lacked** — dry run by default, a ceiling, refuses past it, logs what it purged.
- **Bulk clear confirms with a count and the promise:** *"Clear 14? They stay in the bin for 7 days."*
- **Clearing a drafted job frees its Draft button** (D51) and removes it from /d; **Restore** puts it back.
- ⚠ **Privacy:** the bin holds résumés — state the 7-day retention and delete securely. The privacy page and `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION` get the line (D44's rule).
- ⚠ **Clear is not Pass.** It means *not now*; it writes no pass and trains nothing.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** clear → in the bin, absent from Queued and /d · restore → back, same state · an 8-day-old item is invisible **and** purged by the sweep · an applied item **cannot** be cleared · removal behaves the same in **every** non-terminal state · the sweep refuses past its ceiling.

### D54 · ⭐ COMPANY-WISE TRACKING — never apply into the same company twice without knowing

Owner: *"company-wise tables for jobs applied or trying to apply to, to avoid applying for different jobs within the same company without track."*

⛔ **The risk:** two or three applications into one employer, each unaware of the others — different roles, different résumés, possibly contradictory answers — read by one recruiter. Today the only guard is the **per-company cap**, which *counts* but does not *show.*

**THREE SURFACES, ONE DATA SOURCE:**
1. **The Table → a "By company" view** (D15). A toggle *List | By company.* Each company is a row — logo · name · *3 roles: 1 sent · 1 waiting on you · 1 queued* · last activity · outcomes (replies, rejections) — that **expands to its jobs** with status and dates (D15's timeline). ✅ It covers **applied AND in-play** (drafted, queued, stopped, ready): *"trying to apply"* counts.
2. **At the point of action.** On **Draft** — card, posting panel, deck — when the company already has any active or sent application, show a **non-blocking notice:** *"You already have 2 roles at Scale AI — 1 sent 28 Sep, 1 queued. Draft this one too?"* ⛔ Never silent, never a hard block — the per-company cap still enforces the limit.
3. **In Draft House.** Queued is labelled by company; D52's Start summary lists the company holds; a stopped card's fold shows the company's other applications.

**⛔ THE COMPANY KEY IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM.** Key by a **stable company identity, not a display-name string.** *"Scale AI"*, *"Scale"* and `scale.com` must be **one** company; **two different companies that share a name must NOT merge.** The *"Localhost"* and *"Physical Superintelligence → Intel"* defects were exactly this. Use the **ATS company id + the company KB + the domain.** ⛔ **Report how companies are keyed today and list the collisions** — one company on two boards, two companies with one name — **before building.** ⚠ A company on Greenhouse *and* Workday is still one company.

**DATA.** Source is `job_applications` plus the apply queue. ⛔ **Depends on D43:** the company id, company and title are **snapshotted into the application record**, so the table survives a deleted posting — build D43 first. ⚠ A cleared item (D53) is **not** an application; **a sent one is, forever.**

**DEFAULTS, so the build is not blocked** (owner may change any): the notice **warns at the SECOND role** at a company that has any active or sent application · **no new block** — the existing per-company cap (Settings → Applying) does the blocking · the look-back for *"already applied"* is **all time for sent, current for in-play**, with the date shown so the user can judge. A hard *"not twice within N days"* rule can be added later.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** two jobs at one company on different boards appear under **one** company row · two same-named companies stay **separate** · drafting a second role at a company **shows the notice** · the By-company counts equal the List view's rows grouped · a deleted posting's application **still appears** (D43) · clearing a queued item removes it from its company's row.

## ⛔ D56–D58 · THE MANUAL PATH — a résumé generated by hand, and then nothing works — 2026-10-07

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (37c lanes), on local `main` `01d575b`, NOT PUSHED** — D55 (a)–(l) (badge, Copy sheet, Report this form, the ring, saved answers, Workday advance, right-click save; migration 136) · D56 (Prepare this application, I submitted it, origin families) · D57 (résumé ready everywhere, Settings list, 90-day retention; migration 131) · D58 (base → tailored pair). Suite on `01d575b`: **3664 / 3662 / 2** (the zip checks — clear at the extension bump). ⚠ No browser pass on the merged stack yet (O82b).

⏸ Queued 2026-10-07 by the owner, with a photo of the extension's tooltip on an Amazon application page (Boston): *"Nothing is prepared for https://account.amazon.jobs. Open the application from your Draft queue."* The owner had **generated a résumé for that job by hand** — and then: **(1)** could not find the résumé on any panel (D57) · **(2)** the ATS did not update (D58) · **(3)** the extension would not fill (D56).

⛔ **The pattern.** The product has **two routes** — *Draft* (the queue) and *manual* (generate by hand) — and only the first was built end to end. The manual route **creates an artifact and then drops it.** D36 walked "MANUAL → `job_applications` with a score" **locally and without the extension**; this is the live version failing at exactly the seams that walk did not cover. **Suggested place in the queue:** D57 beside D51 (the same family: an action of the user's own that cannot be found afterwards); D56 beside D52; D58 after D54.

### D56 · ⛔⛔ THE EXTENSION SAYS "NOTHING IS PREPARED" — for a job whose résumé the user generated

⛔ **Two different causes, and the tooltip names one of them: the ORIGIN.** Amazon's posting lives on `www.amazon.jobs`, but the application lives on **`account.amazon.jobs`** — a **different origin.** The extension matches a packet **by origin**, so a packet keyed to the posting's origin **cannot match the application page, even for a job that IS in the queue.** *And* a manually generated résumé has **no packet at all.** Probe both and report which fired:

1. **What packet exists for this job** — if any — and which origin(s) it is keyed to.
2. **How the extension looks it up** — by origin alone, or by job id — and what it sends.
3. **Does the manual route build a packet at all?**

**THE FIX:**
- **A packet belongs to a JOB and lists its ORIGINS.** `origins[]` = the posting's origin **plus the ATS adapter's known apply origins** (Amazon: `www.amazon.jobs` → `account.amazon.jobs`). The extension matches on *origin in the list* **and**, where the URL carries one, the **job id.** ⛔ **The list comes from the adapter, never from the user** — a packet holds personal data, and **it must never be filled into an origin outside the list.**
- **The message tells the truth in three cases — and never says *"from your Draft queue"* to someone on the manual route:**
  - *a packet exists but this page is not one of its addresses* → say so plainly: *"This page isn't one of this application's addresses."*
  - *no packet, but the page matches a job the user has a résumé for* → **"Prepare this application"** — one click builds the packet on demand (the server maps the page's ATS + job id to the user's job).
  - *no match* → *"draft doesn't know this job — capture it first"*, with the capture button (D23).
- ⭐ **The manual route produces a packet.** Generating a résumé from the posting panel makes that job **prepared** (résumé + resolved fields), fillable **without a Draft.** *Draft is the queue for batches; manual is a one-off — both must fill.*
- **"Mark as applied" on the manual route** — in the popup, the review overlay and the posting panel — so a hand-submitted application creates the `job_applications` row **with the tailored score** (D55 row 8's *"I submitted"*, extended to jobs that were never drafted).
- ⚠ **A packet expires (~10 minutes).** One prepared when the résumé was generated will have lapsed before the user opens the portal — so *Prepare this application* must always be available, never a dead end (D52).

⛔ **Fixture first:** add a **two-origin application to `scripts/fakeAts.js`** (posting host ≠ apply host) — the Workday replica D55 adds is single-origin and would never have caught this.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** a job whose application is on a second origin → the packet matches · a manual résumé → the extension fills it, no Draft involved · each of the three messages appears in its case · **a packet is never filled outside its origin list.**

### D57 · ⛔ A MANUALLY GENERATED RÉSUMÉ CAN BE FOUND NOWHERE

The owner generated a résumé for a job and *"couldn't find it when I went back, across all panels."* ⛔ **The same class as D51** — an action of the user's own, with no trace afterwards.

**PROBE — report:** where the generation wrote the résumé (which table, which user, which job) · whether it was **shown once and never stored** · whether the **quota decremented** (*"a Draft or a new résumé uses one"*) for something the user then cannot reach · and **which panel is supposed to list it** — because today none does.

**THE FIX — a résumé is attached to its job and shows up where the job is:**
- **The posting panel's Résumé button changes state** (the D51 pattern): *Résumé ready · 2h ago — view · download · regenerate* — never a button that offers to generate again while hiding the one that exists.
- **A small marker on the job card** — *résumé ready* — in every view (it is one card, D46).
- **A list of every generated résumé** in **Settings → Your data → Generated résumés** (the `34 kept` row), per job, with date, download, delete.
- **Once the job is drafted or applied, the résumé follows it** into Draft House and The Table (D15/D16). ⛔ **"Kept" means kept** — a stored résumé is retrievable after a reload and after a month.
- ⚠ **Retention for a résumé not tied to an application:** it is a *convenience copy*, not evidence — default **90 days** (A57's rule), **kept for good once the job is drafted or applied**, shown on the item (*"expires in 40 days"*). *Owner may change the 90.*

⛔ **Tests:** generate by hand → the posting panel shows *résumé ready* after a reload · it is listed under Settings · drafting the job carries it to Draft House · deleting it frees the button · a generation that fails to store **refunds the quota and says so.**

### D58 · THE ATS DID NOT UPDATE AFTER THE RÉSUMÉ WAS GENERATED

The owner generated a tailored résumé and the job's score **stayed on the base résumé's.** The score should now describe **the résumé that would be sent.**

- ⭐ **Score the generated résumé** with the same deterministic scorer (`scoreAtsLocally` — **zero model calls**, D17) and show **base → tailored:** *"Base 58 → tailored 71."* ⛔ **If the tailored résumé scores LOWER, say so** — it can, and hiding it would be the very thing the score exists to prevent.
