The owner pasted the stored text of an imported **RTX posting (Marlborough, MA)**. The description is **raw HTML** — `<p style="text-align:left"><b>Date Posted:</b></p>2026-08-26…` — with the quotes **backslash-escaped** in places (`style=\"…\"`), and it opens with a block of **label : value lines**: *Date Posted · Country · Location · Position Role Type · a citizenship / immigration-status line · Security Clearance Type · Security Clearance Status.* *"We should be able to handle these as well."* **Suggested place in the queue:** after D41 — it feeds D42's location fixtures, D41(d)'s US evidence and D48's deck strip.

⛔ **Today the tags show as literal text — which means the panel ESCAPES the description, and that is why it looks broken.** The tempting fix is to *render* the HTML, and **that would open a stored-XSS hole**: captured and crawled descriptions are third-party content, and a captured job lands in the **shared** pool, so a hostile page would run its markup in **every** user's browser. ⛔ **The fix must not trade ugliness for a vulnerability.**

**1 · MARKUP → STRUCTURED TEXT, deterministic (D17), done at INGEST and re-checked at RENDER.**
- Decode entities (including `&lt;p&gt;`-style escaped HTML) and **unescape the stray `\"`.**
- Convert through an **allow-list** — `p br ul ol li b strong i em h1–h6 a` — into **blocks** (paragraphs, lists, bold headings) that the posting panel renders **as React elements, never as injected HTML.** Everything else is dropped; `style`, `on*`, `script`, `iframe` and `javascript:` links never survive.
- ⛔ **Test with a hostile fixture:** a description carrying `<script>`, `<img onerror>` and a `javascript:` link renders as **inert text.**
- It applies to **every source** — capture, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday — one normaliser, not one per adapter. Report how many stored descriptions today contain `<p`, `&lt;` or `\"`.

**2 · LABEL BLOCKS → FIELDS.** A leading run of *Label: value* lines is **structured data in prose clothing.** Parse it with a **vocabulary of known labels**, take the fields, and **remove those lines from the body** so they are not shown twice. Vocabulary to start: *date posted · country · location · position / role type (Onsite · Hybrid · Remote) · citizenship / immigration status · security clearance type · clearance status · relocation assistance · travel · requisition id · employment type · pay range.* Unknown labels stay in the text.
- **Date Posted** → the deck's *Posted* cell — the **posting's own date**, not the crawl's.
- **Position Role Type: Onsite** → the **workstyle tag** (D29) and the deck's *Workstyle* cell (D48) — and it raises the workplace tag's **47.5%** coverage.
- ⭐ **`Country: United States of America` is POSITIVE US EVIDENCE** (D41(d)): a capture carrying it must be **accepted**, not refused or called ambiguous.

**3 · CODED LOCATIONS.** `US-MA-MARLBOROUGH-MA2 1001 Boston Post Rd BLDG 2` is **`country-state-CITY-sitecode` + a street address.** Parse it to **US · MA · Marlborough · site `MA2`** · street kept apart. ⛔ **THE TRAP, and it is D42's exact bug: the string contains "Boston" — as a STREET (`Boston Post Rd`).** A substring matcher tags this job *"in Boston"* when the city is **Marlborough.** Make it a D42 fixture. ⚠ Whether Marlborough counts as **Greater Boston** is a product call, not a parsing one — it is a **metro** question, never a **city** one.

**4 · CITIZENSHIP AND CLEARANCE ARE FIRST-CLASS FACTS — surfaced, never decided.** Postings state hard eligibility constraints that no score captures. Tag them:
- `us_citizenship` ∈ **`citizen_only`** (*"U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance"*) · **`us_person`** (*"U.S. citizen, national, permanent resident, refugee or asylee"* — export-control wording) · **`none_stated`.** ⛔ **They are different and both exclude F-1 / OPT and H-1B holders.** Do not collapse them.
- `clearance` ∈ none · public trust · Secret · Top Secret · TS/SCI · plus **polygraph**, and **status**: *active required* · *interim acceptable* · *ability to obtain.*
- **Where it shows:** a muted *Requirements* row under the deck strip — *U.S. citizens only · Secret clearance · interim OK* — as **status pills** (non-interactive, D48's rule), **never folded into the ATS score.**
- **A filter option** behind *+ add*: *hide roles that require clearance or citizenship.*
- ⛔ **At Draft** (D51's notice): *"This role requires U.S. citizenship and an active Secret clearance. Your profile doesn't state either — draft will stop and ask."* ⛔ **The product never answers or infers the candidate's eligibility** — the resolver stays exact-or-blank (D36).

**5 · DO NOT BREAK THE GRADES.** ⛔ **A76's blind-file grades and the enrichment imports are keyed on `content_hash`, which is a hash of the description text.** Rewriting stored descriptions **changes every affected hash and marks graded rows stale** — and the owner's grading (O69) is **still pending against the current text.** ✅ **Store the normalised text in a NEW column (`description_text`)** and leave `description` untouched; readers prefer the new one. ⚠ **The scorer reads the description, so this changes scores** — raw HTML adds noise terms (`text-align`, `left`) and label lines add words that are not requirements. **Re-measure ρ and the bands after the backfill, and say how many rows moved.**

**6 · FIXTURES — real postings already seen in this project:**
- **RTX** (this text) — raw HTML, label block, coded location with `Boston Post Rd`, *citizen_only*, Secret.
- **Northrop Grumman** — *CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes · CLEARANCE TYPE: Polygraph · TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time · RELOCATION ASSISTANCE.*
- **Lockheed Martin** — *"active TS/SCI clearance"* in running prose, no label block.
- **Blue Origin** — *Export Control Regulations: U.S. citizen or national, permanent resident, refugee or asylee* → **`us_person`**, not `citizen_only`.
- a **hostile** description (the XSS fixture).

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** the RTX text renders with **no visible tags and no `\"`** · the label block becomes fields and **does not also appear in the body** · `Boston Post Rd` is **not** the city · `citizen_only` and `us_person` stay distinct · the hostile fixture is inert · `description` and `content_hash` are **unchanged** after the backfill · a capture with `Country: United States of America` is accepted.

### D60 · ⛔⛔ NO PILLS — PERMANENTLY BARRED FROM ALL FUTURE DESIGNS

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (38e), `6ddde18`, local.** ~100 capsules in `client/src` → marks (`styles/mark.js`, `.mark`: radius 6, logo face 10.5px, a 3px leading bar over a 12% tint — the sketch's `.mkr`), depth boxes, `.mark-count`, radius-2 meters, radius-12 fields; the deck's segment radius 10 / 7. ⭐ The top nav's tabs were radius 14 on ~26px — a capsule a ≥ 100px scan misses — now depth boxes in the logo face, active filled accent; re-measured in Chrome (`d69NavPass.mjs`): fits at 360 / 390 / 440 / 1280. D59's Requirements row is marks. Guard `test/d60NoPills.test.js` (50% / ≥ 100px / `rounded-full` unless a circle; `client/src` + `extension/` incl. injected CSS; the D63 hold list emptied in `bb21c9c`); D48's allowance withdrawn; the rule in `BRAND.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. ⚠ Before/after screenshots in both themes NOT taken past the first board shots (memory).

Owner: *"I want the pill design to be permanently barred from all future designs."* The offenders in the shots: the **"résumé ready"** capsule on the job cards and in the ATS panel · the **"Strong"** capsules · the orange **"ATS REPORT | HISTORY (1)"** capsule tabs · the orange **"Import jobs"** capsule in the `+` view.

**THE RULE.** **No capsule — no fully-rounded shape — on any element:** tag, badge, status, chip, tab, button, banner, toast, count. ⛔ This **supersedes D48's allowance** (*"pills are for non-interactive tags and status"*) — **that allowance is withdrawn.** The only round shapes left are **perfect circles** — avatars, state dots, the today ring.

**WHAT REPLACES THEM:**
- **Interactive** → a **depth box** (D1), radius 11–12.
- **Status and tags (non-interactive)** → a **mark**: a rectangle, **radius 6–8**, flat (a hairline, no drop), text in the **logo face at ~11px**, a **3px leading bar** in the status colour — or plain coloured text. **Never a filled capsule.**
- **Tabs** → depth boxes in the logo face, the active one filled accent — **not** an uppercase condensed face.
- **Segmented controls** → one rounded rectangle (radius 10) holding rectangular segments.
- **Counts** (the nav's `2`, *10 left*) → a small rectangle, radius 6.

⛔ **THE EXTENSION IS COVERED TOO.** The in-page autofill badge is a capsule today — `.pill { border-radius: 999px }` in `extension/autofill-badge.js` — so it is the first thing this rule changes (see the sketch `extension-latest.html`).

⛔ **A GUARD, so it cannot creep back:** a test that fails on any `border-radius` of 50% of the element's height or more (`999px`, `9999px`, `100px`…) **outside an allow-list** (avatar, dot, ring), scanning `client/`, `extension/` **and CSS injected by `executeScript`** — the badge's CSS lives inside a JS template string, so a stylesheet-only scan would miss it. **Record the rule in `BRAND.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s standing design rules** so no later agent proposes a pill.

### D64 · ⭐ AUTOMATED CAPTURE — a job page is captured, checked against the board, and migrated with no click

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (38b), local, NOT pushed** — `dfc6737` (server) · `21dd8f7` (extension). Against the seven points: **(1)** opt-in, off by default; `chrome.permissions.request` at the user's click in Settings, `remove` when off; `optional_host_permissions` only — ⚠ **five PUBLIC POSTING HOSTS** (`boards.greenhouse.io`, `job-boards.greenhouse.io`, `jobs.lever.co`, `jobs.ashbyhq.com`, `apply.workable.com`), **not** "the D67 family table": that table names gated portals (Workday, Amazon…), and a standing grant there would break the handoff's documented activeTab-only access to sites the user signs in to → owner call **O83 (b)** · **(2)** nothing leaves the browser unless the page is a posting (URL shape, else in-page JobPosting JSON-LD) — zero requests otherwise, tested against the real `background.js` · **(3)** relevance on the server BEFORE any write — US (the capture's own gate), the active profile's role key + roleScopeExtra, an existing row's own buckets; ⛔ an irrelevant posting leaves **no row anywhere** (not even the refusal a manual capture records); fit is not a gate (the board does not hide by fit) · **(4)** origin `auto_capture`, attached not starred; the popup's *Captured today: N* with an undo (fetched when opened — D23) · **(5)** ⛔ nothing fills or submits; *Apply now* is D56's Prepare → Fill, each a click — **auto-prepare on the posting is NOT built** (it would spend a Draft slot with no click) · **(6)** one per URL per user per day, 30 an hour, kill switch `auto_capture_disabled` (app_settings row, else env `AUTO_CAPTURE_DISABLED`) → 403 · **(7)** manual capture unchanged. **Compliance:** privacy page section + storage list (seven), MANIFEST_RATIONALE, PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION rows, STORE_LISTING storage field, AUTOFILL_TARGET §8.6a (the reversals marked); ⏸ the Web Store single-purpose text — at the release (F 4). Tests +20, each guard red when removed. ⚠ **Not run in a real Chrome** → O83 (a).

Owner 10-07: *"phasing out manual capture and building an automated one that auto captures when a tab is opened and captures content runs a check if it is relevant to the user's board, and migrates it without the user having to do anything — and if the user chooses to apply then and there, this would enable us to deliver the payload then and there."*

⛔ **This REVERSES three recorded decisions** — say so in the commit and in `AUTOFILL_TARGET.md` §8.6: **decision A** (*one gesture per application*), the **HELD-OFF per-ATS auto-start**, and the **refusal of auto-saving on LinkedIn / Indeed** (*"needs access to those sites on every page"*). The owner has decided; the build carries the guard rails that made those calls cautious:

1. **Opt-in, off by default.** A setting *Capture job pages automatically* that, when turned on, requests **`optional_host_permissions`** at runtime (`chrome.permissions.request`) for the **job-site origin list only** — the D67 family table plus the boards draft already reads. ⛔ **Never `<all_urls>`**, never in the install-time manifest. Turning it off removes the permissions.
2. **Nothing leaves the browser unless the page IS a posting.** A local pre-check on the page (`JobPosting` JSON-LD, or a known ATS posting URL shape from the family table). A non-posting page sends **nothing** — not the URL, not a hash.
3. **Relevance is decided on the server, against the user's board** — the same D41 gates the board uses (US admission, the active profile's role family, fit) — and **an irrelevant posting is discarded server-side and never stored.** The relevant one goes through the ONE capture gateway (A62/D33) exactly as a manual capture does: dedup, US gate, enrichment, no second path.
4. **Migrated means on the board, silently, with a mark** — *Captured automatically* — and the popup lists *Captured today: N* with an undo per item (D53's bin).
5. **"Apply now" delivers the payload on that page.** If the tab is the application form (or becomes it), the packet is prepared right then (D56's *Prepare*) and the badge offers **Fill** — ⛔ **the fill still takes the user's click** and **Submit is never pressed** (D36). Auto-capture is not auto-apply.
6. **Rate-braked** — one capture per URL per user per day; a cap per hour; a kill switch beside `fullAutoDisabled()`.
7. **Manual capture stays as the fallback** until D64 has been seen working on real attended pages (O73); then the *Capture* button is demoted, not deleted.

⛔ **Compliance before the store:** a privacy-page section (what is read, when, that non-postings send nothing, the off switch), a `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION` row, a `MANIFEST_RATIONALE` entry for the optional host permissions, and the Web Store *single purpose* text rewritten fresh (with F 4). LinkedIn / Indeed pages: **only if** the posting-detection and the server's refetch rules allow it — a page the server cannot refetch is captured from the user's own view, never by draft fetching it with the user's session.

⛔ **Tests:** a non-posting page sends nothing (assert zero requests) · an irrelevant posting stores nothing · a relevant one lands on the board through the gateway · with the setting off, no content script runs · the permission request names only the family origins · the fill still waits for a click. Measured against the local fake ATS only.

### D65 · ⭐ WORK HISTORY AND SKILLS COME FROM THE RÉSUMÉ IN THE PAYLOAD

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (38c), local** — `1d216c7` (+ the active-profile widening in `217926d`). `services/payloadResume.js`: the résumé the packet CARRIES (its `resumes` artifact, else the active profile's base résumé, else the account's) parsed by the renderer's own `buildStructuredResume`; the parse stored WITH that résumé (**migration 138**, `parsed_json`/`parsed_basis` on `resumes`, `profile_base_resumes`, `base_resume`), re-parsed only when its text changes. A payload résumé is the ONE source of work history and its skills — no profile fallback beside it; a parse that reads nothing fills nothing there and says so; claimed skills (`confirmed_skills`) added, deduplicated, listed in `skillsClaimed`, filled even when the parse fails. `attachPacketResume` re-reads the entries when it attaches a résumé after the packet was built. All four of the row's tests, red when the fix is removed. ⚠ *"Have you worked here?"* (D55 f) still reads the base résumé when the packet's autofill payload is built before its résumé is known.

Owner 10-07: *"work history and skills would come from the parsed résumé currently being used to apply, the one in the payload. If that needs a migration that's what we'll do. The user might claim some skills and these should be filled in."*

- **Source of truth for the fill:** the résumé the packet carries (tailored, or the base under D66) is **parsed** into work history (employer, title, dates, location, bullets), education and skills, and that parse is what the extension fills into *Add Another* sections and skills fields. ⛔ Not the profile's stale copy, not a model call (D17 — parsing is in-house).
- **Store the parse with the artifact** — a migration if needed (e.g. `resume_parsed_json` on the generated résumé / base résumé row, written once when the résumé is written, re-parsed when it changes). The packet references it; it does not copy it.
- **User-claimed skills:** a profile list of skills the user claims that the résumé may not show; they are **added** to the fill's skills (deduplicated, never removed by the parse), marked as the user's own claim.
- *"Have you worked here before?"* (D55 f) reads the same parse — the company is in the payload résumé's work history → *Yes*; otherwise leave it for the user (never guess).
- ⛔ **Tests:** the fill's work-history entries equal the payload résumé's parse · a tailored résumé that dropped a role does not resurrect it · a claimed skill appears in the fill · a parse failure fills nothing for those sections and says so.

The extension's origin re-check becomes a generic `(origin, pathPrefix)` scope check (still no ATS parsing — d23's rule); every other family's prefix is `/`. ⭐ **Found while designing → A95:** the LEARNED table can already learn a shared multi-tenant host — the same hazard through the side door. Every packet-address check reads the per-user families. ⏸ **(1) THE MANUAL SWEEP — NOT DONE (O84):** each row must come from an OBSERVED redirect, which means clicking through real postings (attended, often signed in); and ⛔ **Workday** is a security call — `wdN.myworkdaysite.com` is shared by every Workday employer, so a family there would release a packet on any employer's form on that host.

Owner 10-07: *"these are things that can be reused cross platform, we could do a manual sweep to cover as many as possible for them to be prepped, and also have a self-learning module which can be saved and shared across the platform."*

### D69 · THREE SMALL ONES

✅ **DONE 10-07 (38c), local** — (a) `a608e25` SpeedyApply's *Archived* → withdrawn, in the import only · (b) `a608e25` below 440px the tabs stack their words; measured in Chrome (`scripts/d69NavPass.mjs`) — every tab fits with no scrolling at 360, 390, 440, 1280, clear of the avatar · (c) `0139ed6` the evidence URL keeps only id-type parameters (`services/evidenceUrl.js`); the privacy page says so.

- **(a)** Import maps SpeedyApply's **Archived → withdrawn** (owner agreed to lane E's 1–3).
- **(b)** At **390 px** the top nav clips **"THE TABLE"** — fix, with a guard at 390.
- **(c)** ✅ **DECIDED by the owner 10-07 (38): keep only the id-type parameters, drop the rest** — the recommendation below, adopted. Build: an allow-list of id parameters on the stored *I submitted* evidence URL; everything else (session / one-time tokens, `utm_*`, `gclid`, emails) dropped before it is written; the privacy text says which are kept. ⛔ Tests: a token, a `utm_*` and an email parameter never reach the row; `gh_jid` / `jobId` / `applicationId` do.
- ~~**(c)** ❓ **"I submitted" — keep the query string? Owner's question, answered 10-07; decision pending.**~~ *Advantages of keeping it:* the exact confirmation page is the evidence (some portals identify the application only in the query — `?jobId=`, `gh_jid=`, `applicationId=`); it tells two applications on one portal apart; it can link straight back to the portal's status page. *Implications:* query strings also carry **session and one-time tokens, tracking ids (`utm_*`, `gclid`) and sometimes the applicant's email** — keeping them stores credentials-like secrets indefinitely as "evidence", widens what a breach exposes, and must be disclosed. **Recommendation: keep an allow-list of id-like parameters (`jobId`, `gh_jid`, `lever-*` ids, `applicationId`, `req`), drop everything else** — the evidence value without the tokens.

## ⛔ D77 · BACKUPS AND A DISK GAUGE WITHOUT RAILWAY PRO — 2026-10-09

⭐ **STATUS 10-08 (38o): PUSHED and LIVE (`412f757`); the volume is now 5 GB (owner resized 10-09), gauge reads 4,469 MB usable; `pullBackup.mjs` WAS run 10-07 (38g); backups pruned 10-08** — ✅ **PHASES 1 + 2 BUILT 10-07 (38g), local, NOT pushed — no migration.** ⚠ **Premise corrected:** `draft-data` is a **1,000 MB** volume (`railway volume list`; statfs 879 MB usable, 47% used) — not the 0.5 GB Free cap; resume-master-data is 5,000 MB. The 481 / 500 ENOSPC was before the owner grew it on 09-29.
- ✅ **RUN 10-07 (38g, late), on the owner's go:** the first download **timed out at 46 of 55 MB** (the CLI's own transfer timeout) — the `.partial` was never counted; the retry **succeeded and verified**: integrity ok · 2,776 postings (1,951 active) · last migration `136_form_reports` (the copy is from 10-07 02:00Z, before 137 shipped) → `draft-backups/` in the owner's home folder, 1 good copy. Fixed after: "last migration" now reads the highest-numbered id, and the verify step's `-shm` / `-wal` sidecars are removed.
- ⭐ **STATUS 10-08 (38o): the pull WAS run 10-07 (38g) — 55 MB, verified, the retry after a CLI timeout succeeded** — **Phase 1 — `scripts/pullBackup.mjs`**, for the owner to run. ✅ **The command, verified in the installed CLI (railway 5.63.3):** `railway volume files --volume draft-data list /backups --json` and `… download <remote> <local>` — a read-only file download, no shell on the container, ⛔ never `railway run`. (Git Bash rewrites a bare `/backups` to a Windows path; the script calls the CLI from Node, which does not.) It picks the newest `*.db` (never the manifest), downloads to a `.partial`, then **opens it READ-ONLY: `PRAGMA integrity_check`, the tables a draft database must have, a non-empty board, its last migration** — a copy that fails is renamed `*.FAILED`, never counted as good; keeps the last **8** good; prints the newest's age and **warns over 3 days**; ⛔ **refuses a destination inside the repository**; reminds that the folder is production data (encrypt the disk). `--list` read the volume: **newest backup 0.8 days old, 55.3 MB**. ⏸ **The download itself was NOT run — the row says the owner runs it.**
- **Phase 2 — the disk gauge** (`services/diskGauge.js`, statfs on the data directory, reusing the backup package's `backupLimits` for the budget): `GET /api/admin/disk` · an **Ops card** (used / free, backups vs budget, largest files, and what **25 more companies** would do) · a **banner on every Admin tab** while amber or red · a **Pipeline Health alert** (amber = warn, red = critical). **Green < 70% · amber 70–85% · red ≥ 85%** (one rule, `toneFor`).
- ⛔ **D74 P3's tranche gate is built on it:** the projection is measured from this database (rows per active company × bytes per row, **plus the backups that copy it**), and **adding a company, enabling one, or a slug-harvest import that adds companies is refused (507) when the projected usage passes 70%** — or when the disk cannot be read. Disabling never waits on it.
- **Tests** `test/d77DiskAndBackups.test.js` (6): the in-repo refusal · a page-corrupted copy AND an orphaned-page copy flagged **by `integrity_check` itself** · a non-draft database flagged · 8 kept, FAILED left · amber 70 / red 85 · the gate refuses past 70% and on an unreadable disk · the enable route 507s, disable passes, and server.js hands the routers its `DATA_DIR` — ⭐ five mutations (refusal, integrity, thresholds, gate, route), each red. `npm test` **3819 / 3819 / 0**.
- **Phase 3 (a Storage Bucket) and the plan upgrade stay the owner's.**

The owner: Railway's **scheduled volume backups and volume alerts are Pro-only** on this account. **Context:** Free and Trial volumes are capped at **0.5 GB** — **that is draft's 500 MB wall** (the 481 / 500 ENOSPC); Hobby is **5 GB**, Pro **50 GB**, and volumes can be **resized live on paid plans.** ⛔ **So today the app's own backups sit on the one volume they are meant to protect**: a lost or corrupted volume takes the database *and* its backups, and D74's growth runs straight into the 0.5 GB cap.

**PHASE 1 · A LOCAL PULL — no new vendor, no plan change.**
- `scripts/pullBackup.mjs`, run by the owner on Windows: copies **the newest app backup** off the volume to a folder **outside the repo** (`C:\Users\duggi\draft-backups\`). ⚠ **The agent verifies the exact command in the installed CLI** — `railway ssh`, or `railway volume files` (Railway documents CLI file management on volumes) — ⛔ **never `railway run`**, which opens the LOCAL database.
- Then, on the **local copy**: `PRAGMA integrity_check`, a table-row sanity check, and **open it read-only** — *a backup never restored is a hope.* A copy that fails is **flagged and not kept as "the good one".**
- Keep the last **8**; **print the age of the newest** and **warn above 3 days.** ⛔ **Refuse to run if the destination is inside the repo.** ⚠ Once real users exist that folder holds personal data — **encrypt it at rest.**

**PHASE 2 · A DISK GAUGE IN ADMIN — replaces the Pro-only alert.** Volume **used / free** (`statfs` on the mount), the **largest files**, and the **backup budget** — **green, amber at 70%, red at 85%**, a **banner** in Admin and a line in Pipeline Health. ⛔ **D74 P3 reads it:** *no company tranche is enabled if the projected usage after it exceeds 70%.*

**PHASE 3 · OPTIONAL — a Railway Storage Bucket for the nightly backup** (S3 API; operations and egress are free; the Free plan includes 10 GB-month). It protects against **volume loss and ENOSPC, not against losing the Railway account**; it adds an S3 client dependency and bucket credentials (new secrets). *Decide after Phase 1 has run a month.*

⛔ **THE OWNER DECIDES:** whether to **upgrade** — *Hobby ($5 / month) gives a 5 GB volume with live resize, which is what D74 needs; Pro ($20 / month) adds scheduled backups and alerts* — and **when.** Also: how long Railway keeps volume data after a plan lapses is **30 days for Free / Trial** — know the plan's status.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** the pull refuses a destination inside the repo · a copy that fails `integrity_check` is flagged · the gauge turns amber at 70% and red at 85% · D74's tranche gate reads the gauge.

## ⛔ D76 · RAILWAY WEBHOOKS — deploy visibility and a volume alert — 2026-10-09

✅ Owner 10-09, after Railway's changelog (*custom headers for project webhooks*). **Why:** **Resume Master's `merge: A82 + A83 + …` deployment shows FAILED in the dashboard and nobody was told**; **O65** (*a push is not a deploy*) was found by accident; and **draft's volume reached 481 / 500 MB once.** Railway project webhooks push **deployment status changes and alert events** (a deployment failed or crashed, an out-of-memory kill, a volume alert, a monitor trigger) to **any URL**, configured **per project across all environments** — so one webhook covers `draft` **and** `resume-master`.

◐ **SET UP 10-07 (38g, late), on the owner's go:** `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` generated locally (36 random bytes, kept in `draft-secrets/RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.txt` under the owner's home folder, outside the repo; set on draft through the CLI's stdin; never printed) · **the project webhook created** (`ec579f62`) → `https://jobsviadraft.com/api/hooks/railway`, events failed · crashed · oom_killed · deployed · removed · VolumeAlert triggered / resolved · Monitor triggered / resolved, production only. ⛔ **Its `Authorization` header is NOT set:** the Railway tool takes no headers and the API refused the CLI's token for `notificationRuleUpdate` ("Not Authorized") — **the owner adds it in the dashboard** (Project Settings → Webhooks → the hook → Custom headers → `Authorization` = `Bearer ` + the file's contents); until then deliveries get 401 (harmless). ⭐ **Found while setting it up:** Railway's event NAMES (`deployed`, `redeployed`, `oom_killed`, `restarted`, `resumed`, `slept`) are not deployment statuses and the parser dropped them — fixed; `oom_killed` is an alarm. Was: ✅ **STEP 2 BUILT 10-07 (38g) ahead of Step 1, local, NOT pushed — migration 143.** Built first because the two unknowns were answerable from Railway's own docs (read through the Railway docs tool, `observability/webhooks`): ✅ **custom headers are real** (up to 20 per webhook, values write-only, sent with every delivery and with *Test Webhook*), and ⛔ **payloads are NOT signed** — the header IS the authentication. The payload is `{ type: "Deployment.<state>", details: { id, commitHash, commitAuthor, commitMessage, … }, resource: { workspace, project, environment, service, deployment }, severity, timestamp }`; delivery retries 3× and counts any 2xx/3xx as success. ⚠ **The volume- and monitor-alert type strings are NOT published** — accepted by family prefix (`Volume…`, `Monitor…`, `Alert…`); any other type is dropped with its NAME logged, so **the owner's *Test Webhook* reveals what Railway actually sends**.
- `POST /api/hooks/railway` (`routes/railwayHook.js`, mounted before the global parser): **`Authorization: Bearer <RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN>`**, constant-time; anything else **401 with no body** (no token on the server = the same 401: off, not open) · its own **16 KB** cap (413) · **60 / minute** per address (429) · `shared/deployEvents.js` keeps **the type, family, state, severity, project / environment / service names, service + deployment ids and the commit hash — never the commit message or author** (a person), malformed ids dropped · ⛔ read-only: one INSERT into `deploy_events`, an empty **204** whether kept or dropped, nothing echoed.
- **Admin → Ops → "Deployments"**: the last event per service — **red** for `failed` / `crashed` and for any volume / monitor alert (one rule, `isAlarm`) — with **this server's commit and latest applied migration** beside it, so a push that did not deploy shows.
- **Tests** `test/d76RailwayHook.test.js` (7): no / wrong header → 401, no body · unknown types dropped, same empty 204 · oversize 413, non-JSON 400 · **no table but `deploy_events` changes** · ids only · the rate limit · `Deployment.failed` → red, read through the shared rule — ⭐ four mutations (auth, the type rule, the cap, the alarm rule), each red. `npm test` **3813 / 3813 / 0**.

A second webhook to Discord / Slack for the human alert is unaffected.

**THE SHAPE IN FIVE LINES:**
1. ⛔ **A VM adds nothing to crawling postings** — the ATS boards are public JSON and the existing adapters stay in charge. **The pilot's two jobs:** **J1 find a company's board** (which ATS and slug — *the volume problem, D74 P3*) and **J2 learn where Apply lands** (D67 part 1, the sweep O84 says needs attended work). **J3 (custom career sites) is out of the pilot.**
2. ⛔ **A worker that cannot reach the database:** it **leases a task** from `GET /api/crawler/next` and **returns a signed result** to `POST /api/crawler/result`. **No DB credentials, no user data, no model call.** Its only secret is `CRAWLER_TOKEN`. **A separate service from the one that will hold user sessions (E3)** — the pilot rehearses that boundary.
3. **Ladder, browser last:** plain HTTP over `/careers` first (`detectKnownAtsMatch` already exists) → **only if empty and client-rendered**, the browser, reading **the network log** (the page's own call to `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>` is the best evidence). **Results go through the existing harvest → `validateBoard` → admin dry-run add. ⛔ Never auto-enabled.**
4. ⛔ **Rules of engagement — the line is ToS and robots, not technique:** **public pages only** · **`robots.txt` honoured** · an **identifying User-Agent** and a public `/crawler` page · **per-host rate limits** · **a fresh context per company** · **never** log in, type, submit, solve a CAPTCHA, evade a challenge or record a query string · **a data-driven, owner-editable DENY-LIST** (`linkedin.com`, `indeed.com`, `glassdoor.com`, `ziprecruiter.com`, `monster.com` …) that wins over every task · a takedown adds a domain the same day.
5. ⛔ **SSRF guard:** task URLs come from untrusted data — refuse `localhost`, private ranges, link-local and the cloud-metadata address, **re-checked after every redirect.**

**BUILD ORDER — so it is working shortly:**

URLs: YouTube searches, Open Library searches, course / article home pages, LeetCode problems — links only, nothing copied.

The HTML stays in `docs/` as the archive; the JSON is what the app reads; re-running the script after the owner edits the HTML updates it (a diff of added / removed IDs is printed). **Verbatim:** titles, goals, notes, checkpoints and definitions unchanged — the owner's words.

## ⛔⛔ D118 · THE ATLAS IS LIVE — content added without a rebuild; counts move as postings arrive and leave — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"we should be able to do this such that when we add to base files of the atlas, that should reflect in production rather than having to rebuild it and the counts and metrics dynamic, as in a new job is ingested featuring python, that should reflect across the postings we show."*

**P1 · COUNTS MOVE WITH THE BOARD (no nightly wait):** when a posting is **ingested, updated, closed or expires**, the same transaction that writes it **re-matches its skills once (the one `postingMatcher`) and adjusts the per-node counts** — `atlas_node_stats` gains / loses that posting (total, per role, per level read, per family) — and writes its D114 spans. Every surface reads those live rows: Atlas pages, the hover popup, Your map, role and family maps, the board's skill tags. **The nightly pass stays as the reconciliation** (a full recount; any drift it corrects is logged as a number, which should be 0). Caches: the peek route and page data are invalidated on a count change (or a 60-second cap), never the old 1-hour cache. ⚠ **The boilerplate fix (pending the owner's yes) belongs in the same matcher** — strip text repeated across a company's postings before counting.
**P2 · CONTENT CHANGES WITHOUT A DEPLOY:** the database is the source of the Atlas's content in production; files are an import route, not the source. (a) **Admin → Atlas → Import content**: the owner uploads the tracker HTML (or the extracted JSON); **the extraction runs in the owner's browser** (the same extractor, compiled for the client — the server never evaluates an uploaded script), the JSON goes to the server, which **validates it against the schema**, shows a **diff** (added / changed / removed steps, items, patterns, concepts — by ID) and applies it on **Apply**; progress keyed on IDs survives. (b) The node editor, Find on Wikipedia, Draft definitions and publish / unpublish already act live — confirm none waits for a restart. (c) The boot import of `content/learn/*.json` runs ONLY on an empty table (first install), never over newer database content. **TESTS:** `d118IngestMovesCounts` (a new posting asking for Python → Python's count +1 on the next read, no nightly) · `d118CloseMovesCounts` · `d118NightlyDriftZero` · `d118SpansAtIngest` · `d118CacheInvalidatedOnChange` · `d118ImportValidatesAndDiffs` · `d118ServerNeverEvaluatesUpload` · `d118ImportKeepsProgress` · `d118BootImportOnlyWhenEmpty`.
**✅ P2 DONE 10-31 (43v) — `509634e` + `1cb7fd0`, PUSHED; migration 198 (`learn_content`, `atlas_changes`).** The Learn content is a versioned row in `learn_content`; every reader (`/api/learn`, progress, step links, Your map's Learn next, the boot imports) reads `learnContent(db)`; `/api/learn` cache 1 h → 60 s. (a) Admin → Atlas → Import content (`adminLearnImport.jsx`): the tracker's data block runs in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe with CSP `default-src 'none'` (no origin, cookies, storage or network) and posts back JSON only; a `.json` file is parsed, never run (shared extractor `shared/learnTracker.js`). `/api/admin/learn` (`requireAdmin`): `GET /content` · `POST /import/preview` (validate field by field, unknown fields refused incl. `__proto__`, ids unique, refs real, links http(s); diff by id; writes nothing) · `POST /import/apply { content, base }` (409 if the content moved since the preview). Apply re-runs the D115 imports; an owner definition still in its old words takes the new words, a typed or accepted one is kept; **progress is never touched** (a mark on a removed id counts again if the id returns). (b) Every curator tool acts live; **one real staleness bug fixed** — the search index and D114's link list were keyed on count + newest second, so publish B / unpublish A in one second left A searchable; now keyed on `atlas_changes` (triggers on `atlas_nodes` and `skill_synonyms`; ⚠ a rebuild of `atlas_nodes` like 194's drops the triggers — recreate them). After a Find on Wikipedia pick, the summary still waits for Refresh Wikipedia / the nightly run (as the panel says). (c) `seedLearnContentIfEmpty` imports `content/learn/*.json` only on an empty table. 6 tests (the 4 named + `d118BrowserExtractsPage`, `d118CuratorToolsLive`); 9 mutations each red. ⚠ The import panel and sandbox were not walked in a real Chrome. **✅ P1 DONE 10-31 (43v) — `fa00545`, PUSHED; migration 199 (`atlas_posting_match`, `atlas_role_level_stats`, `atlas_live_state`, the queue `atlas_posting_dirty`).** `services/atlas/atlasLive.js`: a posting's change is read ONCE by `postingMatcher` (new `read(p)`: counted + linked nodes in one pass) and its old contribution subtracted / new added — node postings, per role, per level, board totals; `atlas_posting_match` stores what each posting added, so a close subtracts exactly that. **Write paths:** triggers on `scraped_jobs` queue every insert / relevant change / delete (any writer, scripts too, is caught on the next read); the crawl upsert + prune, `ingestJob`, live-search write-back, `runExpiredJobsCleanup`, dedup retire / restore, `boardAge.retireRows`, import revert, the manual close, detail fetch, the description backfill, the level read and enrichment import / revert also drain it in their own transaction. Every surface (peek, node page, Your map, role page, D114 terms) drains first. The nightly `computeAtlasStats` is the recount and logs `[Cron] atlas drift: N`. Peek `max-age` 3600 → 60; server-side page / peek data ≤ 60 s and dropped on a counts-version or `atlasChangeCount` change. **Measured on a copy (2,616 forced active, 609 nodes):** ingest + update median 11.3 ms (OpenAI, 565 postings) / 6.8 ms (4 postings), close 9.6 ms; a boilerplate threshold crossing re-reads that company's affected postings (4 of 40 ingests); **drift 0** after the baseline and after 60 writes. 6 tests (5 named + `d118PerIngestCost`), 13 mutations red; the lane 767 / 767 over 83 files; 158 / 158 re-run on `main`; boot smoke `latestApplied 199_atlas_live_counts`. **Not live:** per family (no family field until D116 M1); pay range, "asked with" and board edges stay nightly; a new node / alias is not a posting write — the nightly reports it as drift with `vocabChanged: true`. ⚠ Found, pre-existing: repeating the full pass in one process slows ≈ 1.3 s → 5–10 s by the third run (heap flat; `main`'s matcher shows the same) — harmless once a day, unprofiled.

## ⛔⛔ D119 · THUMBNAILS — every resource shows what it is before you open it — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"there are links all over for books, videos etc., but no thumbnails, mere text, thumbnails take it to the next level."* **One resolver, one tile component, used by Learn (D115/D117 items), Atlas resources (D105), D114's popup and Your map's Learn next.** No model (D17).
**P1 · WHERE EACH PICTURE COMES FROM (by item kind / URL):** **video with a watch URL** (youtube.com/watch, youtu.be) → YouTube's own thumbnail for that video id + its title / channel from YouTube oEmbed · **video that is a YouTube SEARCH link** (the tracker's `yt()` helper makes many of these) → there is no single video, so **no thumbnail is invented**: a draft tile *"YouTube · search: <query>"* with a play glyph; Admin → Atlas → Learn gets **"Pin a video"** per item (paste a watch URL → the real thumbnail); the agent reports how many video items are search links vs watch links · **book** → Open Library's search API (title + author) → its cover id → the cover image, shown with *"Cover: Open Library"*; no match → a typographic book tile (title, author, the part's colour) · **article / course / guide / sandbox / practice / game** → the page's own share image (`og:image`, else `twitter:image`) fetched server-side (descriptive User-Agent, 5 s timeout, ≤ 2 MB, robots.txt honoured), else the site's icon on a tile in the item kind's colour with the domain.
**P2 · STORED, NOT HOT-LINKED:** each picture is fetched once, resized (≤ 480 px wide, WebP), stored in draft's asset store keyed by URL hash, refreshed monthly with the dead-link check (D105 P6); a failed fetch keeps the tile fallback. **Admin can hide any picture** (one press) — the takedown path. Pictures are **never** placed in documents (résumé, PDF, cover letter).
**P3 · THE TILE (one component, `ResourceTile`):** picture (16:9 video, 2:3 book, square for sites) · kind badge (Video · Book · Game …; rounded square, never a pill) · title · source · *optional* / *new* tags · its C8 state (*opened* — never *done*) · the whole tile is the link (opens in a new tab and records the D117 C8 *opened*). Grid that wraps (fluid, no fixed widths), lazy-loaded images with the title as `alt`; four themes; contrast themes add a solid outline.
**TESTS:** `d119WatchUrlThumbnail` · `d119SearchLinkNoInventedThumb` · `d119PinAVideo` · `d119OpenLibraryCover` · `d119OgImageStoredNotHotlinked` · `d119FallbackTile` · `d119AdminHide` · `d119NeverInDocuments` · `d119TileRecordsOpened` · `d119OneTileComponent`.

**P1 · SOURCES, AS THEY STAND (chat assistant's search 10-31 — the agent re-checks before importing):** **DOL OFLC LCA disclosure files (quarterly) — the primary, current source:** filings, status (certified / withdrawn / denied), job title, SOC code, worksite, **wage offered vs the prevailing-wage level (I–IV)**. **USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub** (approvals / denials, initial vs continuing): public reports in 2026 say its downloadable files stopped after FY2023 and that the hub went offline in March 2026, while some university pages describe data through FY2025 — **the agent checks what is published now and imports the latest complete year, always labelled with its year**; never presented as current when it is not. **E-Verify:** no bulk source — shown only when known (the posting says it, or an admin records it with a source); never guessed.

## ⛔⛔ D122 · ONE OBJECT, ONE COMPONENT — every page shows the same job, the same résumé, the same buttons — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"consistency of modularity across the platform. when i click on a job or resume for a specific job or a specific object, it is a single object and its instances should point towards a single object. currently one page says the job has a resume, one doesn't, one resume viewer features the editor another one doesn't. also the same with use of functions and buttons and designs we use across, like the utility draft logo buttons, and anything else."*
**THE RULE:** each object — **Posting · Application (a user's relation to a posting: status, its résumé version, form, emails) · Résumé version (base / tailored for one application) · Profile · Company · Atlas node · Learn piece** — has **ONE read path** (one server function / route) and **ONE view component** with modes (card · row · detail); **what a view can do comes from the object's own state, never from the page it sits on.** E.g. *"this job has a résumé"* = `application.resume_version_id` read through one function by the board, Draft House, The Table, the job page and the extension alike; **the résumé viewer shows the editor whenever the version is editable by this viewer** (a tailored version not yet submitted, or a base résumé), on every page.
**P1 · AUDIT FIRST (no changes):** `docs/OBJECT_MAP.md` — for each object: its read function(s), every component that renders it, every page that uses them, and **every divergence** found (two answers to "has a résumé", viewers with / without the editor, duplicated job-detail renderers …), each with file:line. `docs/UI_PRIMITIVES.md` — the shared pieces (**DepthButton** — the utility draft-logo buttons · **CompanyBubble** — the bubble standard · the status ring · the fan / card · SectionHeading · drawers · toasts · empty states · ResourceTile, D119) and **every hand-rolled copy** of one. The owner glances at both; then:
**P2 · CONSOLIDATE, worst first:** (1) the résumé's state and viewer (one `ResumeView`, the editor rule above) · (2) the job's detail (one `JobView`, every entry point — D102's "same detail everywhere" made true) · (3) buttons → DepthButton, bubbles → CompanyBubble, cards → the fan · (4) the rest of the audit's list. **No feature work rides on this lane.**
**P3 · GUARDS so it stays fixed:** a test that each object's state is read through its one function (a second query for "has a résumé" fails CI) · a lint guard: no ad-hoc styled `<button>` in `client/src` where DepthButton applies, no second bubble / card implementation · **an admin "Components" page** that renders every primitive in all four themes — the visual inventory. **TESTS:** `d122OneReadPathPerObject` · `d122ResumeStateSameEverywhere` · `d122ResumeEditorRuleFromState` · `d122OneJobView` · `d122NoAdHocButtons` · `d122OneBubbleOneCard` · `d122ComponentsPageRenders`.

## ⛔⛔ D117 · LEARN AS A CIRCLE — the course broken into pieces that each stand alone and each stay part of the whole; start anywhere, go back to understand, go forward to grow — 2026-10-31 (VISION RECORDED; design next, with the owner)

✅ Owner 10-31, on D115's tracker: *"it is a very extensive material source very rich and resourceful but feels like a one directional one one cant get a grip on. it can be tweaked to be a full circle, kinda like the movie arrival, where the circles represent completeness and that there is no beginning and end. what i mean is that the elements of this can be broken into pieces and be curated to cater its audience while it still remains a piece of the whole thing. one can start it from the beginning and go all the way, they should be able to do that, but also begin somewhere and go backwards to make sense of stuff they dont understand or forwards to progress, and it should be meaningful and seamless either way. it should be further enriched to enable exactly this, with guided directions as needed. lets start these, i want these to be a standout feature."*
**What this row fixes now (design follows in a sketch):** (0) ⭐ **D116 M8 binds this design** (owner 10-31: *"when they complete a course they can unlock these"*): every piece must say **which Atlas nodes it teaches**, and completing a piece (its required items done + its checkpoints explained) is what **unlocks** those nodes on Your map — so the piece ↔ node link is part of D117's data, not an afterthought; (1) **every step is a self-contained piece** — entered from anywhere (the Atlas, a posting's hover popup, Your map, search) and readable alone; (2) **every step knows its neighbours in BOTH directions** — *"Before this"* (what it assumes: the steps and concepts it builds on) and *"After this"* (what it opens) — so a learner can walk backwards to make sense of something or forwards to grow; (3) **the linear path from Step 1 stays** as one way round the circle, never removed; (4) **guided directions** — short routes through the pieces for a purpose (*"Make sense of Kubernetes"*, *"Backend → senior"*, *"Get ready for system design interviews"*), each a list of existing steps, so the content is curated per audience without being rewritten. ⚠ **The prerequisite links are the new data this needs** — the tracker's order gives "after" for free; "before" (what a step assumes) must be added per step. How (owner by hand, the chat assistant drafting for his review, or derived from the concept index's step pointers) is decided with the sketch. **Not built until the owner picks the design.** D115 P5 (exercises, games, practice sites) is planned inside this design.

**✏ D117 DESIGN, SKETCHED 10-31 (owner: *"d117 and also d115 p5 and the exercises and other curated materials (exercises, games, books) planned"*) — sketch `learn-circle.html` (built on his real tracker: 108 steps, 373 items, 324 checkpoints, word for word), data file `learn-d117-data.json`; PENDING his look.**
**C1 · THE PIECE (the unit; every step becomes one):** `id · title · goal · part / phase (where it sits on the whole) · items[] (with kind; optional flag) · checkpoints[] · needs[] ("Before this") · opens[] ("After this" = the inverse of needs, computed, never stored) · teaches[] (Atlas nodes — D116 M8's unlock link)`. A piece is **readable alone** and always says *"Part 4 · Distributed systems · one piece of the whole"* and *"piece 54 of 108"*. **Finished** = every non-optional item done AND every checkpoint marked *explained* (the tracker's own rule). Progress per user, server-side (D115 P3).
**C2 · WHERE THE LINKS COME FROM (measured 10-31 on the real data):** **teaches[] — DERIVED, free:** the concept index points 385 terms at the step that teaches them; **105 of 108 steps teach ≥ 1 indexed concept** → D116 M8's piece ↔ node link needs no writing (the concept nodes resolve to Atlas nodes through the thesaurus; a node a step's title names also counts). **needs[] — NOT derivable:** scanning each step's text for concepts another step teaches gives a before-link for only **28 of 108** (0.3 per step) — too thin. → **The chat assistant DRAFTED needs[] for all 108** (2–3 each, from the subject matter; e.g. *System design ← Distributed systems, DNS/HTTP/TLS, Inside a database*; *Transformers ← Neural networks, Language processing, Linear algebra*); **checked: no loops**; 32 pieces open nothing (they round off their part). **Status `drafted`, for the owner's review** in Admin → Learn (*Accept · Edit · Reject* per piece, *Accept all* after reading) — the same pattern as D105 P11's definitions; a link may point FORWARD on the path (e.g. *Computer graphics ← Linear algebra*, which comes later) — that is the circle. File: `learn-d117-data.json` → `needs_drafted`, `teaches_derived`.
**C3 · THE CIRCLE (the overview; the Arrival idea):** all 108 pieces as small rounded squares on one ring, in path order, grouped into the 8 parts as coloured arcs with their names; **filled = finished, half = started, open = not yet**; **choosing a piece draws chords inside the ring** — orange to what it builds on, blue to what it opens; its title and *"piece n of 108 · 3/5 done · 1/3 explained"* in the centre. **A route is drawn as one ink stroke** looping through its pieces, numbered (reduced motion: drawn at once). No beginning and no end: Step 1 is just one place on the ring.
**C4 · THE PIECE PANEL:** where it sits · title · goal · progress · **Before this** (each with its state; **"Go back to understand: <the first unfinished piece it builds on, at any depth>"**) · **After this** · the items grouped by kind (Video … Practice · **Exercise** · **Game**), each ticked when done, links only · **checkpoints** with *"I explained it"* · **"Finishing this unlocks on your map: Kubernetes, Docker …"** (D116 M8; on finishing: *"Unlocked on your map: …"*, the chips fill; *"They go on your Profile only if you add them"*).
**C5 · GUIDED ROUTES — computed from the links, never hand-listed:** a route = **a target set → everything it builds on (recursively) → ordered so nothing comes before what it builds on** (ties: the circle's own order); it **starts at the first piece the user hasn't finished**, with Previous / Next. Seeded routes: *The whole circle* (path order, Step 1 → 108) · *Make sense of Kubernetes* (11 pieces) · *Backend → senior* (26) · *System design interviews* (28) · **From your map: senior ML** (the D116 route's skills → the pieces that teach them: 38) · **"Make sense of…"** — type any concept (*hash table, TLS, attention*), the route to the piece that teaches it is built on the spot. Verified headless: every route ends at its target and never places a piece before one it builds on. **Routes are data** (`learn_routes`: name, targets[]) so the owner can add audiences without code; the D116 route is per user.
**C6 · ENTRY FROM ANYWHERE:** the Atlas page of a node (*"Learn it: …"*), D114's hover popup, Your map's "Enter the course here", search, a D110 interview gap — all open **the piece** (never the start of the path), with its Before / After so the learner can go either way.
**C7 · TESTS (when approved):** `d117FinishedRule` · `d117OpensIsInverseOfNeeds` · `d117NeedsNoCycle` (import refuses a loop) · `d117RouteClosureOrdered` · `d117RouteStartsAtFirstUnfinished` · `d117GoBackPicksDeepestUnfinished` · `d117TeachesFromIndex` · `d117UnlockToastAndMap` (with D116 M8) · `d117DraftedNeedsNotLiveUntilAccepted` · `d117EntryOpensPiece` · `d117CircleStatesFilled` · `d117ReducedMotion` · `d117FourThemes`.

**✅✅ D117 — APPROVED 10-31** (owner on `learn-circle.html`: *"approved but make a progress bar the user may not mark themselves complete"*). **Reference sketch: `learn-circle.html`** (the owner saves it to `docs/sketches/`); this row wins where they differ; C1–C7 stand, **amended by C8 below — there are NO self-ticks**: the sketch's item checkboxes and "I explained it" buttons are replaced by C8. *(Chat assistant's reading of the owner's line: completion must not rest on the user marking it; if he meant otherwise, he corrects it here.)*
**C8 · PROGRESS IS EARNED, NOT TICKED — one progress bar per piece, filled only by what the user actually does:** (1) **Opened** — an item counts as opened when the user opens it **from draft** (draft records the click-out: piece, item, time; no tracking on the other site). Shown honestly as *"opened"*, never *"done"* — draft can't know a video was watched. (2) **Explained** — each checkpoint has a box: the user **writes the answer in their own words** (private; ≥ 25 words; pasted text of ≥ 25 words is refused with *"put it in your own words"*); saved with the date; editable. No model reads or grades it (D17) — the act of writing it is the evidence, the way the tracker meant *"answer out loud as if teaching a friend"*. (3) **Built** — a piece with a required **Build / Project** item takes **a link to what was built** (a repository, a demo; D109's proof link, stored there too). (4) **Verified practice (later, optional, per site)** — where a practice site offers a public profile or API (e.g. Exercism, Codewars), the user may connect a username and draft reads only the count of completed exercises for the linked track; never a password. → **THE BAR** = opened required items × 30 % + checkpoints explained × 50 % + build linked × 20 % (pieces with no required build: 40 % / 60 %); **FINISHED = every required item opened, every checkpoint explained, and the build linked where one is required** — only then does the piece fill on the circle and **unlock its nodes on Your map (D116 M8's "learned" uses THIS rule)**. Optional items (all of D115 P5's games and exercises) add to the bar's "extras" count, never block finishing. **Nothing a user can press says "complete".** The circle's states follow the bar: open (0) · half (> 0) · filled (finished). **TESTS:** `d117NoSelfCompleteControl` (no button or checkbox sets an item or a piece done) · `d117OpenedOnlyFromDraftClick` · `d117ExplainedNeedsOwnWords` (< 25 words refused; a paste of ≥ 25 words refused) · `d117BuildLinkRequiredWhereBuild` · `d117BarWeights` · `d117FinishedRuleC8` · `d116UnlockUsesC8` · `d117OptionalNeverBlocks` · `d117ExplanationsPrivate` · `d117NoModelReadsExplanations`.

## ⛔⛔ D116 · YOUR MAP — the Atlas home, built from the user's résumé: what you have, what grows you to the next level, adjacent domains, branches — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"it need not be a search only empty board, atlas can feature a profile specific board for the user based on their resume. stuff they have, stuff they can explore, like natural progression related skills kinda to advance to senior levels, or branches or adjacent domains so forth and so on."*

**ALL COMPUTED FROM DATA DRAFT ALREADY HAS — no model (D17):** the user's Profile skills (D101, from the résumé parse) · the board's per-node counts (D105 P3) · the `used_with` / `requires` edges (P9) · each posting's real level (`level_read`, D106) · the user's target role(s) from their job profile.
**THE FIVE SECTIONS (signed in; each item a node bubble — the bubble standard — opening its page; each section capped at 12 with "see all"):**
1. **You have** — the user's skills that are Atlas nodes, grouped by kind, each with *"asked for in 940 open postings"*.
2. **To reach the next level** — for the user's target role: **skills whose share of that role's postings rises from the user's level to the next** (e.g. entry/early → mid, mid → senior; share in next-level postings minus share in current-level postings, ≥ 10 points, ≥ 20 postings at each level), not on the profile, ranked by the rise. Line: *"In 61 % of senior Backend postings vs 22 % of mid"*. **This is the "natural progression to senior" — measured from the board, not opinion.**
3. **Adjacent** — `used_with` neighbours of the user's skills that are not on the profile, ranked by demand (*"Often asked with Kubernetes and Go"*).
4. **Branches** — other roles where the user already covers ≥ 40 % of the role's top 15 required skills: *"You cover 9 of 15 for Data Engineer — missing: Spark, Airflow, dbt …"*, ranked by coverage, then demand.
5. **Learn next** — the D115 steps that teach the top gaps from sections 2–4, with the user's progress on each.
**Signed out / no résumé:** the home shows search, **Learn** (D115), and **Explore by role** (the board's biggest roles, each opening its role page with its top skills) — never an empty search page. A one-line prompt: *"Upload a résumé and this page becomes your map."*
**Refresh:** on profile change and nightly after the board stats. **Thresholds are constants in one file** (10 points, 20 postings, 40 %, 12 per section) so they can be tuned from real use.
**SKETCH FIRST:** the chat assistant sketches the home (`atlas-your-map.html`) for the owner before the UI is built; the agent builds the computation and its API (`GET /api/atlas/me`) now.

**THE MAP (owner 10-31, after `atlas-map-options.html`; sketch `atlas-map-combined.html` — PENDING his look):** *"im leaning towards families map, with a hint of the older map … we should make these best things come together. and also similar map for each roles and family would be great in their respective atlas pages."* → **the Families layout with the first map's look, every position a measurement:** five family wedges (ML · Systems · Infra · Data · Backend — a node's family is a stored field, assigned once per node in the admin editor) · the user's skills on the inner ring of their family · **every other node's distance from the centre = how close it is to the user** (share of its postings that also ask for 2+ of the user's skills; dashed guide rings at 80 / 65 / 50 %) · **size = postings** (toggle: size by the rise toward senior) · **ring = have / rises toward senior for the user's role / other** · a family label shows *"you have 3 of 9"* and lights that direction. **Clicking a node shows the owner's three chosen facts:** (1) *"Prometheus is asked for in 280 open postings, and 57 % of those also ask for two or more skills you have"* (the grid's sentence) · (2) *"System design: 22 % of mid ML postings, 61 % of senior (+39 points)"* (the slope's sentence, with a small mid→senior bar) · (3) *"MLflow: step 3 of 8 on your route to senior ML Engineer; 79 % close to what you know, so it comes early"* (the climb's sentence) — plus dashed lines to the user's skills it is asked with, and **Enter the course here** (D117). **The same map on every ROLE page** (centre = the role; distance = share of that role's postings asking for the skill — core in, specialist out; signed in, rings show have / missing) **and every FAMILY page** (centre = the family; distance = share of postings asking for any skill in the family). The rest of Your map (the five sections) stays as sketched in `atlas-your-map.html`. **TESTS (when approved):** `d116MapDistanceIsCloseness` · `d116MapSizeIsPostings` · `d116ThreeFacts` · `d116RoleMapDistanceIsShare` · `d116FamilyMapDistanceIsShare` · `d116FamilyFieldStored`.

**✏ THE MAP, REVISED 10-31 (owner on `atlas-map-combined.html`):** *"love the idea but the map still looks cluttered and like a flight radar, we want it as a neural network kinda thing we can manoeuvre but is not too complicated, so having labels that would traverse us to specific points like we travelled through the neural network looks cool. but love the set up lets stick with this, just concentrate on the map."* → **the set-up stays** (families, closeness, size = postings, the ring, the three facts, Enter the course here); **the drawing becomes a layered network:** columns left → right = **You · Your skills · Very close (≥ 75 %) · Close (60–75 %) · A stretch (< 60 %)** (closeness bands), rows = the five families; edges = *asked with* (You → your skills → the skills each is asked with); edges faint until a node is chosen, then **its path back to You lights** (You → the skill of yours → it). **Manoeuvre:** drag to pan, wheel / pinch / + − to zoom, labels appear as you zoom in (always for the chosen node and its path). **Waypoints that travel:** a row of labels — *You · Your skills · Next up · Toward senior · ML · Systems · Infra · Data · Backend* — each **flies the view** to that point; **"Fly my route"** travels step by step along the route to the user's aim, the side panel following. Reduced motion: jumps instead of flights. Sketch `atlas-map-network.html` (10-31) — **PENDING his look**; the same drawing serves role and family pages (centre = the role / family). **TESTS (when approved):** `d116NetColumnsAreClosenessBands` · `d116NetRowsAreFamilies` · `d116NetPathLightsBackToYou` · `d116NetWaypointsFly` · `d116NetReducedMotionJumps`.

**✏ THE MAP IN 3D, 10-31 (owner: *"i would prefer this in 3d … the traversal in 3d needs to be crisp"*, then on the first 3D try: *"this is still a 2d graph with 3d nodes. try main node in center, other nodes arranged around with adjacent skills and stacks placed close together so they can link. and a pulsing label of the family somewhere. the labels below are redundant they're already above"*) — sketch `atlas-map-3d.html` (three.js r128 from cdnjs), PENDING his look:** **You at the centre**; each family is a **cluster in its own direction** around You (a faint family-coloured aura marks it); **distance from You = closeness** (your skills ≈ 13 units, then 17 + (100 − closeness) × 0.5 — verified headless: 81 % → 24.6, 40 % → 44.6, no overlaps); a small force layout (repel, pull along *asked-with* links, hold to the family's direction, hold to the target distance; seeded, so the same data gives the same map) keeps linked skills together; **one pulsing family label per cluster** (*"INFRA · you have 5 of 8"*), which flies into the cluster; the in-scene column and family headers are removed (the waypoint row above the map does that job). **Blocks:** the bubble standard as glossy toy blocks (rounded square, clear-coat, dark outline, status ring; block colour = family), gentle bob, pop on hover. **Camera:** full orbit round You, slide, zoom; eased flights that arrive looking back toward You; slow turn when left alone; reduced motion → jumps, no bob, no turn. **WebGL unavailable → the 2D network.** **Readability fixes (owner 10-31: *"the map is meaningful but not readable, the square bits doesn't help cause they have no label in 3/4 axes. when i click on a family having a list on the adjacent screen next to map would help readability"*):** every block **turns to face the camera** (billboarded), so its face and name read from any angle · **every skill's name is always shown**, faded and shrunk with distance (nearer = larger and solid), the chosen one bold · **pressing a family fills the side panel with that family's list** — your skills first (by postings), then the rest from closest to furthest, each row *"81 % close · 380 postings · +23 toward senior"*; hovering a row lifts its block; a row flies to it, with **← Back to the family list**. **TESTS (when approved):** `d116Net3dBlocksFaceCamera` · `d116Net3dNamesAlwaysShown` · `d116Net3dFamilyListOrder` · `d116Net3dBackToFamily` · `d116Net3dDistanceIsCloseness` · `d116Net3dSeededLayoutStable` · `d116Net3dFamilyLabelFlies` · `d116Net3dFallback2d` · `d116Net3dReducedMotion`.

**⛔ THE MAP'S CONTRACT — WHAT EVERY DESIGN MUST CARRY (owner 10-31: *"remember that anything i approved or liked as a metric should be retained and presented"*). Whatever the drawing, these stay, measured, visible:** (1) **closeness** — *"Prometheus is asked for in 280 open postings, and 57 % of those also ask for two or more skills you have"* (the sentence, verbatim pattern) · (2) **postings** — how many open postings ask for each skill (*"what skills have more postings … a very good metric"*) · (3) **mid → senior** — *"22 % of mid ML postings, 61 % of senior (+39 points)"* · (4) **the route** — *"Step 3 of 8 … 79 % close to what you know, so it comes early"* · (5) **families** — grouping, *"you have 3 of 9"*, a **pulsing family label**, and **the family's list beside the map** on press (yours first, then closest to furthest) · (6) **the ring** — have / rises toward senior / other, on **the bubble standard** (rounded square, one ring) · (7) **links** — *asked with*, and **the path back to You** when a skill is chosen · (8) **travel** — labels / waypoints that take you to a place (*You · Your skills · Next up · Toward senior · the families*) and **Fly my route** · (9) **Enter the course here** (D117) · (10) the five sections below the map, the role-page and family-page versions of the map. **Rejected as drawings (not as metrics):** the ring radar, the 2D layered network, the 3D cloud (*"not readable"*), the subway / zoom-hubs / carousel set (*"these look dull"*), the deck hand (*"I don't really dig this design"*). ## ⛔⛔ D114 · ATLAS TERMS IN THE POSTINGS — a published term in a job description is a quiet link; hovering shows what it is and that it leads to learning — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-31: *"there also needs to be embeddings through out the job postings wherever these words are, for example the kubernetes word was published successfully, but needs to be earmarked as described, doesnt necessarily need to be marked or underlined but hovering needs to give a small popup to it meaning and signaling it is a learning resource link."* *("Embeddings" here = links embedded in the text — plain text matching against the Atlas and its thesaurus, no vectors, no model, D17.)*

**P1 · WHICH WORDS (server-side, per posting, cached):** a span is linked only when **(a)** it resolves through `skill_synonyms` / the Atlas `alias_of` edges to a **published** node, and **(b)** the scorer already extracted that skill for THIS posting (the posting's own skill list is the allowlist — so "go to market" never links Go, and "React to incidents" never links React). Longest match first ("machine learning engineer" before "machine learning"); whole words only; case-insensitive except the ambiguous short terms (`AMBIGUOUS_TERMS`, one- and two-letter names), which need the exact case. **Only the FIRST occurrence of each term per posting** is linked. Output: `[{start, end, slug}]` over the plain description text, returned with the posting (`GET …/postings/:id` gains `atlasSpans`); recomputed when a node is published or unpublished and nightly with the board stats. ⛔ No change to the description text itself.
**P2 · WHERE:** every place draft shows a posting's description — the board's job detail, the job page's Job tab (`/app/job/:id`), Draft House's "The job" leaf (D113 UI U4), the extension's ATS panel when it shows the description. ⛔ **Never** in documents (résumé preview, PDF, cover letter — never themed, never annotated), never on the company's own page (the extension does not rewrite third-party pages — a separate owner decision if ever wanted).
**P3 · AT REST: no mark** (the owner's call). **On hover / focus:** the cursor becomes a pointer and a faint dotted underline appears under that word only. **Keyboard:** each linked term is a real link (`<a href="/atlas/<slug>">`, in the tab order); focus opens the same popup. **Touch:** a tap opens the popup (no navigation); the popup's link navigates. ⭐ *Assistant's addition (accessibility):* **Settings → Appearance → "Show learning links"** (off by default) draws the dotted underline at rest — ✅ **kept by the owner 10-31 ("yes to all three")**.
**P4 · THE POPUP (small, ~280 px, D92 surfaces, four themes, never clipped):** the term and its kind (*tool · skill · role*) · **one or two lines of meaning** — the node's own definition, else the first sentence of its Wikipedia summary marked *"From Wikipedia"* (CC BY-SA, D105) · *"Asked for in 312 open postings"* · signed in: *"You: on your profile"* / *"Not on your profile yet"* (D101) · a book-mark glyph + **"Learn it in the Atlas →"** (the signal that this is a learning link) and, when the node has one, its first resource (*"Official docs"*). Opens after 300 ms of hover, stays while the pointer is on the word or the popup, closes on leave / Escape; one popup at a time. Data from `GET /api/atlas/peek/:slug` (name, kind, one-line meaning, count, first resource; public, cached 1 h), fetched on first hover, never preloaded for the whole posting.
**P5 · MEASURE:** count popup opens and Atlas visits from a posting (no content, no user id in the count) — the evidence of whether this is used.

**TESTS (mutation-checked):** `d114OnlyPublishedNodes` · `d114OnlyPostingsOwnSkills` (a term in the text but not in the posting's skill list is not linked) · `d114AmbiguousNeedsExactCase` ("Go" links, "go" does not) · `d114LongestMatchFirst` · `d114FirstOccurrenceOnly` · `d114TextUnchanged` · `d114NeverInDocuments` · `d114NoMarkAtRest` (unless the setting) · `d114KeyboardFocusOpens` · `d114TapOpensNotNavigates` · `d114WikipediaAttributed` · `d114PeekLazy` · `d114UnpublishRemovesSpans` · `d114FourThemes`.

**🟡 43u (10-31, night) — D114 BUILT, `6c71d79` (migration **193_atlas_link_counts**), local, NOT pushed** (so production has no popups yet — they arrive with the push). All fourteen tests in `test/d114AtlasInPostings.test.js`, **mutation-checked**: eight rules broken one at a time, each red, bytes restored (the left word edge had no test until "ArGo" was added). **Three deviations, each measured or forced:** **(1) P1(b)** — only **801 of 2,616** local postings carry `skills_json`, so a list-only rule leaves two thirds of the board unlinked: with a list the node must be on it; without one, the Atlas's own counting rule (the words in the text; the scorer's ambiguous words never) and a capitalised single-word name only in its own case ("React", never "react to incidents"). **(2) P1 output** — `[{start, end}]` offsets over the plain text do not survive `formatPosting` (the body is redrawn as blocks), so `GET /api/atlas/terms/:jobId` answers each node's FORMS and one shared pure linker (`shared/atlasLinks.js`) finds them in the text as each surface draws it; the text is unchanged (`d114TextUnchanged`). **(3) P2** — Draft House's "The job" leaf and the extension's ATS panel draw NO description text, so nothing to link there: **no `extension/` change, no zip, no version bump**. Built on: board job detail + deck card (`PostingPanel`), the expanded board card (`JobCard`), the job page's Job tab (`JobWorkspacePanel`; the workspace now returns `postingId`). ## ⛔⛔ D113 · REMOTE AUTO-APPLY — the cloud worker runs on its own; picks arrive by message; one tap sends — 2026-10-31

✅ Owner 10-30/31, after Tsenta: *"we need to have a remote full auto, tsenta currently have one that runs without us having to do anything in the cloud, and they send a text relay of picks that the user can thumbs up to and the system does its thing, so periodically the system runs new ingested jobs against the users profile and sends out these picks in the text and email as needed and it runs independently."* Then: *"I agree with the recommendations."*

**THE THREE ANSWERS:** (1) **A tap on Apply in a picks message = SEND.** No second review; questions the worker can't answer still come back. A setting **"Show me the form before sending"** (off by default) restores the review. (2) **Channels: email + Web Push now; SMS after carrier registration** (US A2P 10DLC or toll-free verification — *assistant's understanding; the agent verifies the current rules and lead time and names the provider before building*); WhatsApp later. (3) **One picks message per run time** (the user's Auto settings), never more.

**THE LOOP (all server-side; the user's computer can be off):**
- **P1 · scheduler** — at each user's run times: new postings since the last run → the user's filters (board filters by default) → **D104** eligibility (unset answers don't exclude) → **D107** liveness threshold → **D106** level → per-company limit + interview pause → ranked by the ATS match → **cut to what the daily cap leaves** → `picks` rows (user, job, run, rank, `line` = D106's one line, expires at the next run). Idempotent per (user, run); a crash never sends twice. **Uses D102 P4's settings — no second settings store.**
- **P2 · picks message** — **"Ask me first":** one email (Resend) + one Web Push per run with the picks (title, company, the one line, **Apply** / **Pass**). **"Apply for me":** no picks message; the picks go straight to the worker and **one summary after the run** ("Sent 4 today; 1 question").
- **P3 · the confirm page** — ⛔ **a link never acts on GET** (mail scanners open links): Apply opens `/p/confirm/<token>` showing the job and ONE **Confirm** press (POST). Token: signed, single-use, bound to (user, pick), **expires at the next run**. Signed in or not, the page shows only that pick. Pass = the same page, "Pass". **Apply all** for the run on the same page.
- **P4 · after the tap** — tailoring starts **only after Apply** (the model cost is spent on jobs the user wants) → the worker (D100) leases it → fills → **sends** → confirmation → Inbox → The Table. A question it can't answer (D100's rules: consent box, human check, unset eligibility, a free-text with no source — D104 P2) → **a message with the question and a link to answer** on the same confirm-page pattern; with Gmail connected (D112) verification codes are read without asking.
- **P5 · SMS (after registration)** — "3 new picks: … Reply 1, 2, 3 or ALL"; replies parsed (numbers, ALL, PASS); **STOP / HELP honoured** as the carriers require; a phone number is verified before use; opt-in recorded with time and wording.
